{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove the sharp spacetime Penrose inequality for smooth one-ended initial-data exteriors in every spatial dimension <i>n</i> ≥ 3, under the dominant energy condition, weak future trapping, the stated differentiated decay and positive enclosing area. These hypotheses force the ADM energy-momentum to be future timelike. Area is the infimum over full enclosing cuts in the original metric. In dimensions three and four, two metric derivatives and one tensor derivative suffice, and both positive enclosing area and future timelikeness follow from the hypotheses.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove the sharp spacetime Penrose inequality for smooth one-ended initial-data exteriors in every spatial dimension <i>n</i> ≥ 3, under the dominant energy condition, weak future trapping, the stated differentiated decay and positive enclosing area. These hypotheses force the ADM energy-momentum to be future timelike. Area is the infimum over full enclosing cuts in the original metric. In dimensions three and four, two metric derivatives and one tensor derivative suffice, and both positive enclosing area and future timelikeness follow from the hypotheses.

- **claim-strong-decay-penrose** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): Let $(\Omega^n,g,K)$ be the smooth one-ended exterior specified above, with integrable constraint densities, finite ADM limits, dominant energy condition and weakly future trapped boundary. Suppose $$g-\delta=O_6(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_5(r^{-1-q}),\qquad \frac{n-2}{2}<q<n-2,$$ and assume $E>\|P\|_\delta$ and $A_{\min,g}(S)>0$. Then $$\label{eq:setting:main} m\geq\frac12\left(\frac{A_{\min,g}(S)}{\omega_{n-1}} \right)^{\frac{n-2}{n-1}}.$$ The coefficient and exponent are sharp in each dimension $n\geq3$.
  - Explanation: Bounds invariant ADM mass by the full enclosing-area infimum, with sharp coefficient and exponent.
- **claim-automatic-future-timelikeness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-automatic-timelikeness)): Assume all hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">3</a> except the inequality $E>\|P\|_\delta$. In particular, retain the one-ended exterior, the $O_6/O_5$ decay with $(n-2)/2<q<n-2$, and $A_{\min,g}(S)>0$. Then $E>\|P\|_\delta$, and Equation <a href="#eq:setting:main" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:main">[eq:setting:main]</a> holds.
  - Explanation: Derives strict future timelikeness while retaining the positive enclosing-area hypothesis.
- **claim-weak-decay-low-dimensions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-low)): Let $n=3$ or $n=4$. Let $(\Omega^n,g,K)$ be the smooth one-ended exterior specified above, with integrable constraint densities, finite ADM limits, dominant energy condition and weakly future trapped boundary. Assume $$g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\qquad q>\frac{n-2}{2}.$$ Then $A_{\min,g}(S)>0$, $E>\|P\|_\delta$, and <a href="#eq:setting:main" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:main">[eq:setting:main]</a> holds.
  - Explanation: Obtains positive enclosing area, strict future timelikeness and the sharp inequality under the weaker differentiated decay in the stated dimensions.
- **claim-prepared-geometric-deformation** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-height-enclosure)): Fix a prepared exterior and $0<\epsilon<1$. For all sufficiently large integers $N$ there is a connected enclosing-set exterior $X_N$, complete with its compact frontier $\Sigma_N$ included, in a smooth Riemannian ambient metric $\widetilde g_N$. It has one Euclidean coordinate end with compact complement, and $$\label{eq:height:enclosure-estimates} \begin{split} &R_{\widetilde g_N}\ge0,\quad R_{\widetilde g_N}\in L^1(X_N), \quad \widetilde g_N-\delta=O_2(r^{2-n}),\\ &R_{\widetilde g_N}=O(r^{-n-\beta'})\quad\text{for some }\beta'>0,\\ &E(\widetilde g_N)\le E_0+P_N(e^{-N\epsilon}+e^{-N\epsilon/2}),\\ &\mathcal H^{n-1}_{\widetilde g_N}(\Sigma_N) \ge e^{-(n-1)\epsilon}A_0. \end{split}$$ Here $P_N$ is a polynomial in $N$, with coefficients depending on the fixed datum and $\epsilon$. The metric is smooth through the frontier. The whole frontier is outer minimizing and locally perimeter minimizing as the boundary of its filled side. It is smooth embedded minimal away from a compact singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-8$; for $3\le n\le7$ the singular set is empty. Its area counts every component.
  - Explanation: Produces actual Riemannian exteriors with controlled energy, full frontier area and nonnegative scalar curvature; the frontier may be singular.
- **claim-prepared-energy-bound** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-numerical-prepared)): Every exterior in Definition <a href="#def:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:prepared">6</a> satisfies $$\label{eq:height:prepared-inequality} E_0\ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_0}{\omega}\right)^{(n-2)/(n-1)}.$$
  - Explanation: Establishes the numerical energy bound for each fixed prepared exterior.
- **claim-strong-decay-end-preparation** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-end-reduction)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ be a smooth one-ended exterior as in Definition <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a>, with compact complement of its coordinate end and with $$g-\delta=O_6(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_5(r^{-1-q}),\qquad \frac{n-2}{2}<q<n-2.$$ Assume integrable constraint densities satisfying $\mu\ge\|J\|_g$, finite ADM limits satisfying $E>\|P\|$, and $\theta_+(S)\le0$ on every boundary component. Suppose that the full-cut infimum of Definition <a href="#def:fullcuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:fullcuts">2</a> is $a=A_{\min}^{g}(S)>0$, and put $m=(E^2-\|P\|^2)^{1/2}$. There are prepared data $(g_j,K_j)$ on the same exterior, with one fixed $\beta\in(0,1)$, numbers $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$, and proper diffeomorphisms $\Phi_j:\Omega\longrightarrow\Omega$ equal to the identity near $S$, such that $$\label{eq:end:reduction-limits} P_j=0,\qquad E_j\longrightarrow m,\qquad \Phi_j^*g\le(1+\epsilon_j)g_j,\qquad A_{\min}^{g_j}(S)\ge(1+\epsilon_j)^{-k/2}a.$$ The positive constant $c_j$ in Equation <a href="#eq:end:prepared" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:end:prepared">[eq:end:prepared]</a> and the end coordinates may depend on $j$.
  - Explanation: Replaces the end by prepared rest data whose energies approach invariant mass and whose enclosing areas retain a lower comparison with the original infimum.
- **claim-boosted-vacuum-charges** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-end-boost)): In the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime of geometric mass $M>0$, let $b,y$ be static time and isotropic spatial coordinates. Make the Lorentz change $$\label{eq:end:boost-coordinates} b=\gamma(T+vx^1),\qquad y^1=\gamma(x^1+vT),\qquad y^a=x^a\ (2\le a\le n),\qquad \gamma=(1-v^2)^{-1/2},$$ where $0\le v<1$. The induced data on $T=0$, oriented by the future normal, have $$\label{eq:end:boost-charges} E=\gamma M,\qquad P_1=\gamma Mv,\qquad P_a=0\ (a>1).$$ The metric and second fundamental form have the homogeneous leading terms computed below, with remainders $O_d(r^{-2p})$ and $O_d(r^{-2p-1})$, respectively, for every fixed derivative order $d$.
  - Explanation: Computes the ADM charges and differentiated remainder orders of a boosted vacuum reference end.
- **claim-compact-constraint-inverses** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-end-compact-inverses)): Let $\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected Euclidean annulus and fix a compact subset of its interior. Smooth scalar sources supported in that subset with zero constant and first moments have smooth symmetric solutions of $\mathsf S(h)=f$ supported in a larger fixed compact subset of $\mathcal A$. Smooth vector sources with zero integrals against every Euclidean Killing field have similarly supported symmetric solutions of $\mathsf D(b)=F$. For $1<a<\infty$ and integers $d\ge0$, these solutions may be chosen linearly with estimates $$\\|h\\|_{W^{d+2,a}}\le C_{d,a}\\|f\\|_{W^{d,a}},\qquad \\|b\\|_{W^{d+1,a}}\le C_{d,a}\\|F\\|_{W^{d,a}}.$$ For arbitrary sources the same conclusions hold after subtracting fixed smooth moment bumps, whose coefficients are bounded by the absolute values of the respective moments.
  - Explanation: Constructs compactly supported linear inverses subject to the affine and Killing moment conditions, with the stated Sobolev derivative gains.
- **claim-sublinear-rescaled-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-end-moments)): Let $h=g-\delta$, $h^{\mathrm b}=g^{\mathrm b}-\delta$, and $b=K$, $b^{\mathrm b}=K^{\mathrm b}$ on their common coordinate tail. Put $H=h-h^{\mathrm b}$ and $B=b-b^{\mathrm b}$. Define the scalar and vector commutators on $\mathcal A_L$ by $$C_L=\mathsf S(\chi_LH)-\chi_L\mathsf S(H),\qquad F_L=\mathsf D(\chi_LB)-\chi_L\mathsf D(B),$$ and their rescaled versions on $\mathcal A$ by $$\widehat C_L(z)=L^2C_L(Lz),\qquad \widehat F_L(z)=L^2F_L(Lz).$$ The flat sources $\mathsf S(H)$ and $\mathsf D(B)$ are integrable. For every fixed affine scalar function $a(z)$ and every fixed Euclidean Killing field $Y(z)$, $$\int_{\mathcal A}a\widehat C_L\,dz=o(L^{2-n}),\qquad \int_{\mathcal A}Y^i\widehat F_{L,i}\,dz=o(L^{2-n}).$$
  - Explanation: Shows that matching charges and integrable flat constraint sources make all rescaled compatibility moments small.
- **claim-strong-decay-strictification** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-end-strict)): Let $\Omega$ be a smooth connected exterior, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and with exactly one Euclidean coordinate end outside a compact set. Let $(g,K)$ be smooth up to $S$, with $g-\delta=O_6(r^{-q})$ and $K=O_5(r^{-1-q})$ for some $q>(n-2)/2$. Choose $0<\beta<\min(1,q)$ and a smooth nonnegative function $B\ge\|K\|_g$ with $B=O_5(r^{-1-q})$. Then the problem $$\label{eq:end:strict-pde} -\Delta_g\phi =B\sqrt{\|d\phi\|_g^2+\varrho^{-2k}}+\varrho^{-n-\beta}, \qquad \partial_\nu\phi=-1\text{ on }S, \qquad \phi\longrightarrow0\text{ at infinity}$$ has a smooth positive solution, unique among decaying smooth solutions. It satisfies $$\label{eq:end:strict-estimates} \begin{gathered} \phi=O_6(r^{2-n}),\qquad \frac{-\Delta_g\phi}{r^{-n-\beta}}\longrightarrow1,\\ \mathfrak f_\phi:=\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{S_R}\partial_{\nu_g}\phi\,dA_g\\ =-\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(S)-\int_\Omega \bigl(B\sqrt{\|d\phi\|^2+\varrho^{-2k}} +\varrho^{-n-\beta}\bigr)\,dV_g<0. \end{gathered}$$ If $K$ is compactly supported, $B$ may be chosen compactly supported. If in addition $g-\delta=O_d(r^{2-n})$ for all $d$, the solution has this decay through every derivative order.* *Suppose also that the ADM limits of $(g,K)$ exist and are finite, that the data satisfy DEC, and that $\theta_+(S)\le0$ on every boundary component. For all sufficiently small $\delta>0$, $$g_\delta=e^{2\delta\phi}g,\qquad K_\delta=e^{\delta\phi}K$$ satisfy $$\label{eq:end:strict-margin} \mu_\delta-\|J_\delta\|_{g_\delta}\ge c_\delta\varrho^{-n-\beta}, \qquad \theta_{+,\delta}<0, \qquad E_\delta=E-\frac{\delta}{\omega}\mathfrak f_\phi, \qquad P_\delta=P.$$ Here $g_\delta\ge g$, and their ratio tends uniformly to one as $\delta\downarrow0$.
  - Explanation: Solves a regularized drift-Poisson problem and uses its negative inner normal derivative and finite flux to strictify the constraints and boundary expansion.
- **claim-strong-decay-positive-shell** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-end-positive-shell)): Assume all hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">3</a> except possibly $E>\|P\|_\delta$. For every $\lambda>0$ there is a smooth function $U_\lambda\ge1$, constant near $S$, such that $$g_\lambda=U_\lambda^{4/p}g,\qquad K_\lambda=U_\lambda^{2/p}K$$ are smooth complete one-ended data with the same $O_6/O_5$ decay and $q$, integrable constraint densities, the dominant energy condition and weakly future trapped boundary, and satisfy $$E_\lambda=E+2\lambda,\qquad P_\lambda=P,\qquad A_{\min,g_\lambda}(S)\ge A_{\min,g}(S)>0.$$
  - Explanation: Raises energy by a prescribed amount while fixing momentum and increasing every full-cut area, without assuming future timelikeness.
- **claim-scalar-curvature-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-scalar-identity)): For every smooth $f,Z$ and every smooth $g,K$ the following identity holds, without a field equation or energy hypothesis: $$\frac12e^{2t}R_{\widehat g} =\mu+J(w)+\mathcal T+w(F)-F\tau-u^{-1}\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g V, \label{eq:scalar:identity}$$ where $2\mu=R_g+\tau^2-\|K\|^2$, $J=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_gP_K$, and $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal T={}&\frac12\|T^0\|^2+\|M+s_pa_wy\|^2 +\left(ks_p-\frac{(k-1)^2}{4}v\right)\|y\|^2+ks_pd x^2\\ &-\frac{k-1}{2k}(F-\chi j)^2+\chi j^2-\chi Fj+F^2 +2s_p\chi j a_w x . \end{aligned} \label{eq:scalar:quadratic}$$ The quantity $\mathcal T$ is smooth, including where $df=0$.
  - Explanation: Gives an exact curvature decomposition before imposing the coupled equations; the quadratic expression remains smooth at graph-gradient zeros.
- **claim-weighted-quadratic-coercivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-scalar-coercivity)): For $0\leq p\leq N$ and $0\leq v<1$ the quadratic form in Equation <a href="#eq:scalar:quadratic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:scalar:quadratic">[eq:scalar:quadratic]</a> is nonnegative, and $$\|T\|^2+\|M\|^2+d j^2+F^2+\|dt\|_{A_d}^2 \leq C_k(1+N)^2\mathcal T. \label{eq:scalar:coercivity}$$ At $dt=0$ one has, with constants depending only on $k$, $$c_k\bigl(\|T^0\|^2+\|M\|^2+F^2+\chi j^2\bigr) \leq\mathcal T\leq C_k\bigl(\|T^0\|^2+\|M\|^2+F^2+\chi j^2\bigr). \label{eq:scalar:stationary-coercivity}$$
  - Explanation: Proves nonnegativity and polynomial weighted coercivity, retaining the degenerating axial weights.
- **claim-floor-exclusion** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-scalar-floor)): There is $c_1>0$ depending on $k$ alone such that, at any point with $dt=0$, $$\mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f) \geq c_1\mathcal T-\mathcal P_N(vF^2+\|K\|^2). \label{eq:scalar:floor-algebra}$$ Suppose a smooth solution on a truncation with outer $f=Z=0$ satisfies the trace equation and has $\|h\|\leq C$ on the core and $\|h\|\leq C\varrho^{-b_1}$ on the end, with constants independent of the homotopy parameter and $N$. One may choose $0<\delta_0<\min(c_1,1)/2$ and a polynomial $C_N$ such that a solution of Equation <a href="#eq:scalar:system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:scalar:system">[eq:scalar:system]</a> for which $\min t=-\epsilon$ cannot attain this minimum of $t$ at an interior point. This holds in both stages of the homotopy.
  - Explanation: Combines minimum-point curvature algebra with height bounds to exclude an interior minimum on the floor of the degree domain.
- **claim-penalty-flux-energy-cost** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-scalar-flux)): Fix $\epsilon$ and $N$ as above. Suppose a smooth global solution of Equation <a href="#eq:scalar:system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:scalar:system">[eq:scalar:system]</a> satisfies $t>-\epsilon$, $Z\leq\mathcal P_N$, and on the coordinate end $$f=O_j(e^{-c_Nr}),\qquad t=O_j(r^{2-n}),\qquad \Delta_gt=O(r^{-n-\beta})$$ for all required derivative orders, with constants allowed to depend arbitrarily on this fixed $N$. These hypotheses will be supplied by Theorem <a href="#thm:elliptic:filled" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:elliptic:filled">19</a>. Then $$\begin{gathered} \mathfrak F_N:=\lim_{r\to\infty} \int_{S_r}g(V,\nu_g)\,dA_g =\int_{\mathcal M_N}u\Xi\,dV_g,\\ \widehat E-E=-\frac{\mathfrak F_N}{k\omega},\qquad \mathfrak F_N\geq-\mathcal P_N(\ell+\ell^{1/2}),\\ \widehat E\leq E+\mathcal P_N(\ell+\ell^{1/2}). \end{gathered} \label{eq:scalar:flux-energy}$$ The polynomial in the error uses only the fixed geometry, the weights, and the explicit parameters, not the arbitrary fixed-$N$ derivative constants in the stated end estimates.
  - Explanation: Identifies the ADM energy change with the global divergence flux and bounds its unfavorable part using polynomial penalty-band estimates.
- **claim-filled-coupled-solvability** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-elliptic-filled)): Fix smooth prepared data satisfying Equation <a href="#eq:end:prepared" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:end:prepared">[eq:end:prepared]</a> on a complete one-ended exterior with nonempty compact smooth boundary. In particular, $K$ is compactly supported, $g-\delta=O_d(r^{2-n})$ for every fixed $d$, $R_g=O(r^{-n-\beta})$ for some $0<\beta<1$, the dominant-energy margin is bounded below by a positive multiple of $\varrho^{-n-\beta}$, and every boundary component is strictly future trapped. Fix $0<\epsilon<1$ and $$\frac n4<b_1<\min\{n-2,n/2\}.$$ Use the filled manifolds $\mathcal M_N$, weights $\rho_0,\rho_1,\rho$, and definitions in Equation <a href="#eq:scalar:variables" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:scalar:variables">[eq:scalar:variables]</a>. Choose $\delta_0>0$ and the polynomial $C_N$ as in Lemma <a href="#lem:scalar:floor" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:scalar:floor">17</a>. For all sufficiently large integers $N>k=n-1$, there are smooth functions $f,Z$ on $\mathcal M_N$ solving Equation <a href="#eq:scalar:system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:scalar:system">[eq:scalar:system]</a>. The associated function $t$ satisfies $$\label{eq:elliptic:polynomial-bounds} -\epsilon<t\le Z\le P(N),\qquad \ell\le l(t)\le e,\qquad \|f\|+\|df\|_g\le \exp(P(N)),\qquad \ell=e^{-N\epsilon}.$$ Here and below $P$ is a polynomial with coefficients depending only on the fixed prepared data, $n$, $\epsilon$, and the fixed choices in the filling. The height $h=\eta f$, $\eta=\ell^{3/2}$, obeys $$\label{eq:elliptic:height-bound} \|h\|\le C,\qquad \|h(x)\|\le C r(x)^{-b_1} \quad\hbox{on the original end},$$ where $C$ is independent of $N$. At each fixed $N$, for every integer $j\ge0$ there are constants $C_{N,j}$ and $a_N>0$ such that on that end $$\label{eq:elliptic:end-bounds} \|D^j f\|\le C_{N,j}e^{-a_Nr},\qquad t,Z=O_j(r^{2-n}),\qquad \Delta_g t=O(r^{-n-\beta}).$$ The constants in Equation <a href="#eq:elliptic:end-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:elliptic:end-bounds">[eq:elliptic:end-bounds]</a>, and higher derivative bounds on compact sets, may depend arbitrarily on fixed $N$.
  - Explanation: Obtains smooth coupled solutions on the filled manifold, with polynomial potential bounds, exponential-polynomial graph bounds and fixed-parameter end decay.
- **claim-uniform-height-and-outer-floor** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-elliptic-height)): There are constants $C$ and $r_1$, independent of $N,R$ and the homotopy parameters, such that every smooth solution of the trace equation in Equation <a href="#eq:elliptic:homotopies" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:elliptic:homotopies">[eq:elliptic:homotopies]</a> satisfies $$\|\eta f\|\le C,\qquad \|\eta f\|\le C(r^{-b_1}-R^{-b_1})\quad(r_1\le r\le R).$$ For each fixed $N$ there is $R_{\min}(N)$ such that $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$ and $Z=0$ on $S_R$ imply $t>-\epsilon$ there. The same conclusions hold in the second homotopy, where in fact $f=0$.
  - Explanation: Bounds normalized height uniformly along the homotopies and excludes the floor at sufficiently distant outer Dirichlet spheres.
- **claim-potential-bound-before-ellipticity** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-elliptic-upper)): Every smooth fixed point on $\mathcal M_{N,R}$ with $t\ge-\epsilon$ satisfies Equation <a href="#eq:elliptic:polynomial-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:elliptic:polynomial-bounds">[eq:elliptic:polynomial-bounds]</a>, with the same polynomial bounds for all $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$ and all homotopy parameters.
  - Explanation: Establishes the common polynomial potential bounds for above-floor fixed points before invoking uniform ellipticity.
- **claim-rankone-gradient-regularity** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-elliptic-gradient)): Let $n\geq3$ and $0<c\leq1$. Let $Q$ be a smooth metric coordinate ball, or a smooth half-ball with constant Dirichlet data on its face. Suppose that $u$ is $C^2$ up to the face and satisfies almost everywhere $$A:\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_g u=G,\qquad A=\mathop{\mathrm{id}}-(1-\chi)e\otimes e,\qquad c\leq\chi\leq1,\qquad e=\frac{\nabla_g u}{\|\nabla_g u\|_g} \quad\text{where }\nabla_g u\ne0. \label{eq:elliptic:rankone-equation}$$ At a zero of the gradient, $e$ may be any measurable unit vector. Assume $\|\nabla_g u\|_g+\|G\|\leq M$. On every smaller ball, including its portion of the Dirichlet face, there are estimates $$_{C^\alpha}\leq C,\qquad \int_{B_r(x)\cap Q}\|\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_g u\|_g^2\,dV_g \leq C r^{n-2+2\alpha}. \label{eq:elliptic:rankone-conclusion}$$ Here $\alpha\in(0,1)$ depends only on $n,c$, and $C$ depends on $n,c,M$, the fixed coordinate geometry and the distance from the other chart boundaries. No modulus of continuity of $\chi$ enters these constants.
  - Explanation: Provides gradient continuity and local Hessian mass control without requiring a continuity modulus for the axial eigenvalue. The displayed conclusion in the supplied text has a missing left-hand expression.
- **claim-natural-growth-holder-estimate** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-elliptic-natural-growth)): Let $n\ge3$ and let $Q$ be a Euclidean coordinate ball, or a smooth flattened half-ball with constant Dirichlet value on its face. Suppose a bounded classical function $Z$ satisfies weakly $$\label{eq:elliptic:natural-growth-model} \begin{gathered} -\partial_i(A^{ij}\partial_j Z)=\partial_i B^i+S, \qquad \lambda I\le A\le\Lambda I,\qquad A=A^{\mathsf T},\\ \|B\|\le C_0,\qquad \|S\|\le C_0(1+\|DZ\|^2+F_0). \end{gathered}$$ where $A$ is measurable and $F_0\ge0$ is bounded for each individual solution. Assume, for some $a\in(0,1)$ and $r_0>0$, and every ball of radius $0<r\le r_0$ with center in the coordinate patch, that the measure $\nu=(1+F_0)\,dx$ obeys $$\label{eq:elliptic:ng-source-morrey} \nu(B_r\cap Q)\le C_1r^{n-2+a}.$$ Then $Z$ has a uniform $C^b$ bound on smaller patches, including the constant-Dirichlet face, for some $b\in(0,a)$. Its exponent and bound depend only on $n,\lambda,\Lambda,C_0,C_1,a,r_0$, the bound for $\|Z\|$, the fixed chart geometry and the distance from the remaining patch boundary. They use neither a modulus of continuity for $A$ nor a uniform pointwise bound for $F_0$ or $D^2Z$.
  - Explanation: Controls the oscillation of a bounded scalar solution with quadratic gradient growth using a uniform source-mass bound and measurable elliptic coefficients.
- **claim-fixed-parameter-smooth-regularity** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-elliptic-regularity)): Fix $N$. Smooth solutions of either homotopy on $\mathcal M_{N,R}$ with $t\ge-\epsilon$ have bounds of every fixed order on coordinate balls and on outer Dirichlet half-balls of a sufficiently small fixed size. Their size and the constants may depend arbitrarily on $N$, but are independent of $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$ and of the homotopy parameter. In particular their $C^{1,\gamma}$ norms are bounded on each fixed truncation, for any chosen $0<\gamma<1$.
  - Explanation: Bootstraps above-floor fixed points to every fixed derivative order with constants uniform in the truncation radius at fixed deformation parameter.
- **claim-arbitrary-trial-trace-solvability** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-elliptic-trial-trace)): Let $\mathcal D$ be a compact smooth $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth boundary, with $n\ge3$ and $k=n-1$, and let $K$ be a smooth symmetric tensor on $\mathcal D$. Fix $N>k$, $0<\gamma<1$, and a positive constant $\eta$. Use $p(t)=N\vartheta(Nt)$ and $l(t)=\exp(\int_0^t p(s)\,ds)$, with the smooth cutoff $\vartheta$ of Equation <a href="#eq:scalar:parameters" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:scalar:parameters">[eq:scalar:parameters]</a>, and define $D$, $t$, $A_\chi$ by Equations <a href="#eq:scalar:implicit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:scalar:implicit">[eq:scalar:implicit]</a> and <a href="#eq:scalar:variables" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:scalar:variables">[eq:scalar:variables]</a>. Put $K_a=aK$. For every $z\in C^{1,\gamma}(\mathcal D)$ and $a\in[0,1]$, the Dirichlet problem $$\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}\left(K_a+\frac l{\sqrt D}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}f\right)=\eta f, \qquad f\|_{\partial\mathcal D}=0, \qquad t+\frac1{2k}\log(1+l(t)^2\|df\|^2)=z$$ has a unique solution $f=f_a[z]\in C^{3,\gamma}$. The solution map is continuous from $[0,1]\times C^{1,\gamma}(\mathcal D)$ to $C^{3,\gamma}(\mathcal D)$ and maps bounded sets to bounded sets. All constants may depend on $N,\eta,\mathcal D,g,K$ and the prescribed bound for $z$. There is no restriction on the minimum of the implicitly determined $t$.
  - Explanation: Solves the trace Dirichlet problem for arbitrary prescribed trials and gives uniqueness and continuous dependence without a floor assumption.
- **claim-negative-height-filling-barrier** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-height-ramp)): The product lengths in the filling can be chosen $O(1+N)$ so that, for some $b_2>0$ independent of $N$, every sufficiently large $N$ satisfies $$\label{eq:height:negative-core} h<-b_2 \quad\text{on the whole added filling and a neighborhood of }S.$$ The conclusion concerns the final solution with the original prepared $K$; no analogous assertion is required along the existence homotopy.
  - Explanation: Chooses filling lengths so the final normalized height remains uniformly negative throughout the filling and near the original boundary.
- **claim-small-height-curvature-control** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-height-curvature)): For all sufficiently large $N$, $$R_{\widetilde g_N}\ge0 \quad\text{on }\Omega\cap\{\|h\|\le b_3\}.$$ On the original exterior the metric satisfies $\widetilde g_N\ge e^{-2\epsilon}g$. Its ADM energy obeys $$\label{eq:height:energy-upper} E(\widetilde g_N)\le E+P_N(\ell+\ell^{1/2}).$$
  - Explanation: Preserves nonnegative scalar curvature on the required small-height exterior while retaining metric domination and the energy upper bound.
- **claim-obstacle-perimeter-minimizer** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-height-bv-existence)): There is a bounded finite-perimeter set $F_N\supset O_N$, modulo null sets, minimizing $P_{\widetilde g_N}$ among all bounded sets containing $O_N$. One may choose it to contain every other minimizer modulo null sets. Its perimeter satisfies $$\label{eq:height:competitor-bound} P_{\widetilde g_N}(F_N)\le e^{P_N}.$$
  - Explanation: Obtains a bounded obstacle-containing perimeter minimizer maximal under inclusion, with an exponential-polynomial competitor bound.
- **claim-obstacle-detachment** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-height-detachment)): For all sufficiently large $N$, $$\label{eq:height:detached} \mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\|D\mathbf1_{F_N}\|\cap O_N=\varnothing.$$
  - Explanation: Excludes contact of the minimizing frontier with the distance obstacle for sufficiently large deformation parameter.
- **claim-three-dimensional-exterior-bound** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-intro-exterior-inequality)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ be an exterior as in Definition <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-class">32</a>. Assume Equations <a href="#n3:intro:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:constraints">[n3:intro:constraints]</a>–<a href="#n3:intro:decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:decay">[n3:intro:decay]</a>, integrability of $\mu$ and $\|J\|_g$, and the finite ADM limits <a href="#n3:intro:energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:energy">[n3:intro:energy]</a>–<a href="#n3:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:momentum">[n3:intro:momentum]</a>. Orient $\partial\Omega$ by the normal into $\Omega$, and suppose $\theta_+(\partial\Omega)\le0$. If $E>\|P\|_\delta$, then $$\label{n3:intro:penrose} \sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2} \ge \sqrt{\frac{a_g(\partial\Omega)}{16\pi}}.$$ No extension of the data across $\partial\Omega$ is required.
  - Explanation: Proves the invariant-mass enclosing-area inequality in the weakly decaying exterior class under future timelikeness.
- **claim-three-dimensional-positive-enclosing-area** (bound, [source](#stmt-bridge-bridge-positive-area)): Let $(\Omega,g)$ be a connected orientable smooth three-dimensional exterior, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $B$ included, with one asymptotically flat end and compact complement. Let $a_g(B)$ be the infimum of the full areas of the enclosing cuts in Definition <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-class">32</a>, including all components and all portions coincident with $B$. Then $$0<a_g(B)<\infty.$$
  - Explanation: Shows that every full enclosing cut has a common positive area lower bound, without using the constraints or trapping signs.
- **claim-three-dimensional-conformal-identities** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-conformal-formulas)): For a smooth function $f$, set $$g_f=e^{4f}g,\qquad K_f=e^{2f}K.$$ The corresponding constraint densities satisfy $$\begin{aligned} 16\pi e^{4f}\mu_f &=16\pi\mu-8\Delta_g f-8\|df\|_g^2, \label{n3:reduction:conformal-energy}\\ 8\pi J_f &=e^{-2f}\bigl(8\pi J+4K(\nabla f,\cdot)\bigr). \label{n3:reduction:conformal-momentum} \end{aligned}$$ Here the second identity is an identity of covectors. Consequently, $$\begin{aligned} 16\pi e^{4f}(\mu_f-\|J_f\|_{g_f}) \ge{}&16\pi(\mu-\|J\|_g)\notag\\ &+8\bigl(-\Delta_g f-\|df\|_g^2-\|K\|_g\|df\|_g\bigr). \label{n3:reduction:conformal-dec} \end{aligned}$$ On the fixed boundary, $$\theta_{+,f}=e^{-2f}(\theta_++4\partial_\nu f). \label{n3:reduction:conformal-expansion}$$ Equivalently, if $u=e^f>0$, the last summand in Equation <a href="#n3:reduction:conformal-dec" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:reduction:conformal-dec">[n3:reduction:conformal-dec]</a> is $8u^{-1}(-\Delta_g u-\|K\|_g\|du\|_g)$.
  - Explanation: Gives the conformal transformation of the physical constraint densities and the future boundary expansion.
- **claim-three-dimensional-strict-direction** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-strict-direction)): Choose $$0<\delta<\beta<\min(q,1).$$ There are smooth positive functions $w$ and $\phi$ on $\Omega$, with $w=r^{-3-\delta}$ on the end, such that $$\begin{aligned} &\partial_\nu\phi=-1\quad\hbox{on }B, &\phi&=O_2(r^{-1}),\label{n3:reduction:strict-boundary}\\ &-\Delta_g\phi-\|K\|_g\|d\phi\|_g\ge w, &\frac{-\Delta_g\phi}{w}&\longrightarrow1. \label{n3:reduction:strict-source} \end{aligned}$$ The Euclidean normal flux $$L_\phi=\lim_{r\to\infty} \int_{S_r}\partial_r\phi\,\,\mathrm dA_\delta$$ is finite and negative. For every finite $s\ge0$, set $$\label{n3:reduction:linear-family} u_s=1+s\phi,\qquad g_s=u_s^4g,\qquad K_s=u_s^2K.$$ These data are complete up to $B$ and satisfy DEC, strictly for $s>0$. If $\theta_+\le0$ on $B$, their boundary expansion remains nonpositive and is strictly negative for $s>0$. Their decay exponent can be taken to be $\min(q,1)>1/2$, their constraint densities are integrable, and $$\label{n3:reduction:strict-charges} E_s=E+sA_\phi,\qquad P_s=P, \qquad A_\phi=-\frac{L_\phi}{2\pi}>0.$$ Their full enclosing infima satisfy $$\label{n3:reduction:strict-areas} a_g(B)\le a_{g_s}(B) \le (1+s\\|\phi\\|_\infty)^4a_g(B).$$ In particular $E_s\to E$ and $a_{g_s}(B)\to a_g(B)$ as $s\downarrow0$. No sign assumption on the ADM vector is needed.* *If $K$ is compactly supported and the metric has symbol estimates of all orders with $g-\delta=O(r^{-1})$, the function can instead be chosen with $\phi=O_k(r^{-1})$ for every $k$, while retaining Equations <a href="#n3:reduction:strict-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:reduction:strict-boundary">[n3:reduction:strict-boundary]</a> and <a href="#n3:reduction:strict-source" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:reduction:strict-source">[n3:reduction:strict-source]</a>.
  - Explanation: Constructs an energy-raising conformal family preserving momentum and enclosing-area comparison, with no original ADM sign assumption.
- **claim-enclosing-area-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-area-compactness)): Let $g_j$ be smooth metrics on the fixed exterior $\Omega$, converging to $g$ locally uniformly up to $B$. Suppose that in a fixed chart outside a compact set they satisfy, with constants independent of $j$, $$\label{n3:reduction:area-geometry} c\delta\le g_j\le C\delta,\qquad r\|\partial g_j\|_\delta\le C.$$ Suppose also that each $g_j$ has an asymptotically flat end, possibly in a different chart, and admits a fixed compact enclosing competitor with uniformly bounded area. Then minimizing filled enclosures exist, their boundaries lie in one fixed compact subset of $\Omega$, and $$a_{g_j}(B)\longrightarrow a_g(B).$$ The perimeter and smooth enclosing infima agree. Each minimizing boundary is $C^{1,1}$, and is smooth minimal away from contact with $B$.
  - Explanation: Keeps minimizing enclosures in a common compact region and proves convergence of their full enclosing infima under receding metric changes.
- **claim-three-dimensional-prescribed-reference** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-boosted-reference)): Let $E>\|P\|$ and $m=(E^2-\|P\|^2)^{1/2}$. There is a spacelike plane near spatial infinity of Schwarzschild spacetime of mass $m$ whose induced data, in asymptotically Euclidean coordinates on the plane, have ADM charges $(E,P)$. The reference data satisfy $$g_*-\delta=O_k(r^{-1}),\qquad K_*=O_k(r^{-2})$$ for every derivative order $k$.
  - Explanation: Matches any prescribed future-timelike ADM vector using a Schwarzschild reference plane with differentiated decay at every order.
- **claim-three-dimensional-compact-inverses** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-compact-inverses)): Let $\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a fixed connected open annulus and let $Q\Subset\mathcal A$. Smooth sources supported in $Q$ admit the following compact corrections, supported in a fixed larger compact subset of $\mathcal A$.* 1. *If $\int f=0$ and $\int x^if=0$ for $i=1,2,3$, there is a smooth symmetric tensor $h$ with $\mathcal Lh=f$ and $\\|h\\|_{W^{k+2,p}}\le C_{k,p}\\|f\\|_{W^{k,p}}$.* 2. *If $\int V\cdot Y=0$ for every Euclidean Killing field $Y$, there is a smooth symmetric tensor $k$ with $\mathcal Dk=V$ and $\\|k\\|_{W^{k_0+1,p}}\le C_{k_0,p}\\|V\\|_{W^{k_0,p}}$.* *The estimates hold for integers $k,k_0\ge0$ and $1<p<\infty$.
  - Explanation: Specializes the compact scalar and symmetric-divergence inverses to the stated annular source class.
- **claim-three-dimensional-sublinear-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-moment-estimates)): For data satisfying Equation <a href="#n3:reduction:original-decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:reduction:original-decay">[n3:reduction:original-decay]</a> and integrable $\mu,\|J\|$, put $h=g-\delta$ and $\pi=K-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\delta K)\delta$. Then $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal Lh&=16\pi\mu+O(r^{-2-2q}),\notag\\ \partial_j\pi_{ij}&=8\pi J_i+O(r^{-2-2q}). \label{n3:reduction:linear-source-integrability} \end{aligned}$$ In particular these Euclidean sources are integrable. Their scalar boundary fluxes paired with affine functions having zero constant term, and their vector boundary fluxes paired with rotational Killing fields, are $o(R)$ on coordinate spheres of radius $R$.
  - Explanation: Obtains integrable Euclidean linear constraint sources and sublinear affine and rotational boundary fluxes from the weak original decay.
- **claim-three-dimensional-annular-replacement** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-annular-replacement)): Suppose $E>\|P\|$, and let $(g_*,K_*)$ be the reference end from Lemma <a href="#n3:reduction:boosted-reference" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:reduction:boosted-reference">38</a>, identified with the given end in the common asymptotically Euclidean coordinates. For all sufficiently large $R$ there are smooth data $(\widetilde g_R,\widetilde K_R)$ equal to $(g,K)$ on $r\le R$ and to $(g_*,K_*)$ on $r\ge4R$ such that $$\label{n3:reduction:annular-deficit} 16\pi(\widetilde\mu_R-\|\widetilde J_R\|_{\widetilde g_R}) \ge-\eta_RR^{-3},\qquad \eta_R\longrightarrow0.$$ The possible negative part is supported in $R<r<4R$. The metrics there are uniformly Euclidean comparable and have uniformly bounded scaled first derivatives. The construction uses no derivatives of the original data beyond those in Equation <a href="#n3:reduction:original-decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:reduction:original-decay">[n3:reduction:original-decay]</a> for its quantitative estimates.
  - Explanation: Joins the original data to the charge-matched vacuum reference with a vanishing annular DEC deficit, using only the original differentiated bounds.
- **claim-three-dimensional-vacuum-bend** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-vacuum-bend)): The data in Proposition <a href="#n3:reduction:annular-replacement" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:reduction:annular-replacement">41</a> can be modified farther out, inside their exact Schwarzschild part, so that they are induced by a constant-static-time slice outside a compact set. This modification adds no constraint deficit. Write $(g_R,K_R)$ for the resulting unscaled data. In the common end coordinates the metrics are uniformly Euclidean comparable, and throughout all transition annuli $$\label{n3:reduction:bend-geometry} \|\partial g_R\|_\delta+\|K_R\|_\delta\le C/r.$$ There is a smooth proper radius $\rho_R$ on the end which equals the original coordinate radius on the gluing annulus and equals the rest isotropic radius beyond the transitions, with $$\label{n3:reduction:radius-geometry} c r\le\rho_R\le C r,\qquad \|d\rho_R\|_{g_R}^2\ge c, \qquad \|\Delta_{g_R}\rho_R\|\le C/r.$$ All transition annuli lie between fixed multiples of $R$; the constants can depend on the prescribed timelike ADM vector, but not on $R$.
  - Explanation: Bends the exact vacuum reference to a static slice without adding a constraint deficit and retains uniform transition geometry.
- **claim-three-dimensional-radial-dec-repair** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-radial-repair)): Consider the data obtained from Proposition <a href="#n3:reduction:annular-replacement" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:reduction:annular-replacement">41</a> and Lemma <a href="#n3:reduction:vacuum-bend" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:reduction:vacuum-bend">42</a>. There is a smooth positive conformal factor $u_R$, constant on the unchanged inner region and tending to one at infinity, such that $(u_R^4g_R,u_R^2K_R)$ satisfy DEC everywhere. Moreover $$\label{n3:reduction:repair-size} \\|u_R-1\\|_\infty=o(R^{-1}),\qquad \|du_R\|=o(R^{-2})\quad\hbox{on the transition region}.$$ The final end is exactly Schwarzschild with $K=0$ and mass $m+o(1)$. The boundary expansion retains its original weak sign.
  - Explanation: Repairs the annular DEC deficit by a positive conformal factor at vanishing mass cost while preserving the boundary expansion sign.
- **claim-three-dimensional-rest-preparation** (construction, [source](#stmt-n3-reduction-rest-reduction)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ satisfy the exterior hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">33</a>, including $\theta_+\le0$ on its smooth compact boundary, and let $m=(E^2-\|P\|^2)^{1/2}>0$. There is a sequence of smooth exterior data $(g_j,K_j)$ on $\Omega$ with the following properties:* 1. *$\mu_j>\|J_j\|_{g_j}$ everywhere and $\theta_{+,j}<0$ on $B$. The constraint densities are integrable. On the end their DEC margin is bounded below by $c_jr^{-3-\delta}$ for some $c_j>0$ and one fixed $0<\delta<1$. For a smooth positive radius extension $\rho$, the constant can be decreased so that $\mu_j-\|J_j\|_{g_j}\ge c_j\rho^{-3-\delta}$ on all of $\Omega$.* 2. *$K_j$ is compactly supported, and in a rest chart $g_j-\delta=O_k(r^{-1})$ and $R_{g_j}=O_k(r^{-3-\delta})$ for every $k$. In particular $\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{g_j}=O(r^{-3})$ there. Their ADM momentum is zero.* 3. *$(g_j,K_j)\to(g,K)$ smoothly on every fixed compact subset up to the boundary, their ADM energies satisfy $E_j\to m$, and $a_{g_j}(B)\to a_g(B)$.* *Consequently it suffices to prove the energy/enclosing-area inequality for the class in <span class="upright">(i)</span>–<span class="upright">(ii)</span> in order to prove Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">33</a> in its stated class.
  - Explanation: Produces strict prepared rest data with smooth local convergence, energy convergence to invariant mass and full convergence of enclosing areas.
- **claim-three-dimensional-unconditional-timelikeness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-weak3)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ satisfy all the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n3:intro:exterior-inequality" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n3:intro:exterior-inequality">33</a> except $E>\|P\|_\delta$. Then $$E>\|P\|_\delta,\qquad \sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}\ge \sqrt{\frac{a_g(B)}{16\pi}},\qquad B=\partial \Omega.$$ No extension of the data across $B$ is required.
  - Explanation: Removes the timelike assumption using the positive conformal family and positive enclosing area.
- **claim-three-dimensional-designated-end-bound** (theorem, [source](#stmt-bridge-intro-global-penrose)): Let $(M,g,K)$ be a connected orientable smooth three-dimensional initial data set without boundary, with $g$ complete. Suppose that outside a compact set $M$ has finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end, in its asymptotic coordinates, assume $$g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\qquad q>\tfrac12,$$ and finite ADM energy and momentum limits with the normalizations <a href="#n3:intro:energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:energy">[n3:intro:energy]</a>–<a href="#n3:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:momentum">[n3:intro:momentum]</a>. The decay exponents may differ between ends. Assume that the physical constraint densities <a href="#n3:intro:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n3:intro:constraints">[n3:intro:constraints]</a> obey $\mu\ge\|J\|_g$ and that both $\mu$ and $\|J\|_g$ are integrable on $M$.* *For every chosen end and every admissible boundary $S$ in Definition <a href="#bridge:intro:global-admissible" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="bridge:intro:global-admissible">46</a>, its ADM vector $(E,P)$ satisfies $$\label{bridge:intro:global-inequality} E>\|P\|_\delta,\qquad \sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}\ge \sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S)}{16\pi}}.$$
  - Explanation: Extends the exterior inequality to complete boundaryless data with finitely many ends using the ambient enclosing class.
- **claim-four-dimensional-designated-end-bound** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n4-thm-weak)): Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be smooth and connected, with $M$ orientable, $K$ an arbitrary smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $S=\partial M$ nonempty, compact, and smooth. Suppose $g$ is complete as a metric space with $S$ included. Outside a compact set let $M$ have finitely many, and at least one, ends diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\mathbb R^4$. Assume $$\mu\ge\|J\|_g,\qquad \mu,\|J\|_g\in L^1(M,\,\mathrm dV_g),$$ and, on every end for a common $q>1$, $$g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),$$ with finite energy and momentum limits <a href="#n4:intro:energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:intro:energy">[n4:intro:energy]</a>–<a href="#n4:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:intro:momentum">[n4:intro:momentum]</a>. On every component of $S$ assume $\Theta_K\le0$, with normal into $M$.* *Then for each end $e$, $$\label{n4:intro:main} E_e\ge \sqrt{\|P_e\|_\delta^2+ \frac14\left(\frac{A_e(S)}{\omega_3}\right)^{4/3}}.$$ In particular $E_e>\|P_e\|_\delta$, and the invariant mass satisfies $$\label{n4:intro:mass} \sqrt{E_e^2-\|P_e\|_\delta^2} \ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_e(S)}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}.$$
  - Explanation: Bounds the energy and invariant mass of each end using the end-isolating enclosing volume and derives strict future timelikeness.
- **claim-four-dimensional-cut-reduction** (construction, [source](#stmt-n4-lem-cut-reduction)): Under the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n4:thm:weak" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:thm:weak">49</a>, the quantity $A_e(S)$ is finite and strictly positive for every end $e$. Truncating all other ends at sufficiently large coordinate spheres gives a connected, complete one-ended exterior $M_T$ with compact smooth boundary $S_T$. All its boundary components have future nonpositive expansion with the normal into $M_T$. Its selected-end charges are the original charges, and $$\label{n4:end:cut-truncation} A_*(M_T,g)\ge A_e(S),\qquad \lim_{T\to\infty}A_*(M_T,g)=A_e(S).$$ The common parameter $T$ in the limit can be replaced by any exhaustion in which every unwanted truncation radius tends to infinity.
  - Explanation: Proves positivity of the end-isolating infimum and reduces other ends by trapped coordinate-sphere truncations, with the required area comparison and exhaustion limit.
- **claim-four-dimensional-conformal-identities** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n4-lem-conformal)): Let $u>0$ be smooth, and set $g_u=u^2g$, $K_u=uK$. In dimension four, as an identity of scalar functions and an identity of covectors, respectively, $$\begin{aligned} u^2\mu_u&=\mu-3u^{-1}\Delta_g u,\label{n4:end:conformal-mu}\\ uJ_u&=J+3K(\mathop{\mathrm{grad}}_g\log u,\cdot).\label{n4:end:conformal-J} \end{aligned}$$ Consequently, $$\label{n4:end:conformal-dec} u^2\bigl(\mu_u-\|J_u\|_{g_u}\bigr) \ge \mu-\|J\|_g+3u^{-1} \bigl(-\Delta_g u-\|K\|_g\|\,\mathrm du\|_g\bigr).$$ For any consistently oriented hypersurface, $$\label{n4:end:conformal-expansion} \Theta_{K_u}=u^{-1} \bigl(\Theta_K+3\partial_\nu\log u\bigr).$$
  - Explanation: Gives the conformal constraint identities, DEC estimate and consistently oriented boundary expansion formula.
- **claim-four-dimensional-positive-shell** (construction, [source](#stmt-n4-end-positive-shell)): For any one-ended data in Theorem <a href="#n4:thm:weak" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:thm:weak">49</a> and every $\lambda>0$, there is a conformal change preserving all its hypotheses, with $$E_\lambda=E+2\lambda,\qquad P_\lambda=P, \qquad A_*(g_\lambda)\ge A_*(g).$$ The conformal factor is constant near the compact boundary and is at least one everywhere.
  - Explanation: Raises energy while preserving momentum, weak trapping and enclosing-volume lower comparison.
- **claim-four-dimensional-prescribed-reference** (construction, [source](#stmt-n4-end-boosted-plane)): For any $E>\|P\|$, put $m=(E^2-\|P\|^2)^{1/2}$. A spacelike plane in the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime of mass $m$, sufficiently far from its central region, has induced vacuum data $(g_*,K_*)$ with charges exactly $(E,P)$, and $$g_*-\delta=O_k(r^{-2}),\qquad K_*=O_k(r^{-3}) \quad\text{for every integer }k\ge0.$$ Here $K_*$ is one half the metric rate in the future normal direction.
  - Explanation: Constructs vacuum reference data carrying the prescribed future-timelike charges with all-order differentiated decay.
- **claim-four-dimensional-compact-inverses** (construction, [source](#stmt-n4-end-compact-inverses)): Fix a compact subannulus $U_0$ of a bounded connected Euclidean annulus $U$. If $f$ and $F$ are smooth and supported in $U_0$, and $$\label{n4:end:compatibility} \begin{aligned} \int f\phi\,\,\mathrm dz&=0 &&\text{for every affine }\phi,\\ \int F_iY^i\,\,\mathrm dz&=0 &&\text{for every Euclidean Killing field }Y, \end{aligned}$$ there are symmetric smooth tensors $b,k$, supported in a fixed compact subset of $U$, with $\mathcal Lb=f$, $\mathcal Dk=F$. For every integer $j\ge0$ and every $1<p_1<\infty$, they can be chosen linearly in the sources so that $$\label{n4:end:inverse-bounds} \\|b\\|_{W^{j+2,p_1}}\le C\\|f\\|_{W^{j,p_1}},\qquad \\|k\\|_{W^{j+1,p_1}}\le C\\|F\\|_{W^{j,p_1}}.$$ The constant depends only on $U_0,U,j,p_1$ and fixed localization choices. The moment conditions are also necessary for compactly supported solutions.
  - Explanation: Characterizes the compatibility moments for compact linear constraint corrections and supplies linear Sobolev estimates.
- **claim-four-dimensional-rest-replacement** (construction, [source](#stmt-n4-prop-rest-end)): Let $(M,g,K)$ satisfy the one-ended hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n4:thm:weak" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:thm:weak">49</a>, and suppose $E>\|P\|$. Put $m=(E^2-\|P\|^2)^{1/2}$. There is a sequence of smooth data $(g_R,K_R)$ on the same manifold, complete with the same compact boundary, satisfying the dominant energy condition and the same future boundary inequality, such that:* 1. *$K_R$ is compactly supported, and the ultimate end is an exact static Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spatial end;* 2. *its energy is $m_R=m+o(1)$, its momentum is zero, and both constraint densities are integrable;* 3. *$A_*(g_R)\ge(1-o(1))A_*(g)$.* *Every error here tends to zero as $R\to\infty$ for the fixed original data and fixed timelike vector. No uniformity as $E-\|P\|$ tends to zero is asserted or needed.
  - Explanation: Replaces a future-timelike end by a static vacuum rest end while preserving DEC and weak trapping and controlling every full cut from below.
- **claim-four-dimensional-fixed-rest-strictification** (construction, [source](#stmt-n4-lem-strictification)): Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected four-dimensional exterior, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary included, with one Euclidean coordinate end and compact complement. Suppose $\mu\ge \|J\|_g$ and $\Theta_K\le0$ on every boundary component, where the boundary normal $\nu$ points into $M$. Assume that $K$ has compact support and that, outside a compact set, $$g=\left(1+\frac{c}{r^2}\right)^2\delta$$ in the end coordinates, for a constant $c$. Fix $0<\delta_1<1$, and extend the coordinate radius to a positive smooth function $r$ on $M$.* *There is a nonnegative smooth function $\phi$, with $\phi=O_k(r^{-2})$ for every fixed derivative order $k$, such that, for all sufficiently small $s>0$, the data $$(g_s,K_s)=(e^{2s\phi}g,e^{s\phi}K)$$ satisfy $$\label{n4:eq:strictification-output} \Theta_{K_s}<0,\qquad \mu_s-\|J_s\|_{g_s}\ge c_s r^{-4-\delta_1} \quad\hbox{on }M,\qquad c_s>0.$$ They are complete, have compactly supported second fundamental form, integrable constraint densities, zero ADM momentum and finite ADM energy. Their end satisfies $$\label{n4:eq:strictification-decay} g_s-\delta=O_k(r^{-2})\quad\hbox{for every fixed }k, \qquad R_{g_s}=O(r^{-4-\delta_1}).$$ For the full enclosing-cut infimum on this fixed exterior, $$\label{n4:eq:strictification-limits} E_{g_s}\longrightarrow E_g, \qquad A_*(g_s)\longrightarrow A_*(g) \quad\hbox{as }s\downarrow0.$$
  - Explanation: Strictifies each fixed rest datum, retaining zero momentum and convergence of energy and enclosing volume as the conformal parameter vanishes.
- **claim-four-dimensional-prepared-transfer** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-n4-end-transfer)): Theorem <a href="#thm:numerical:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:numerical:prepared">8</a>, applied in dimension four, implies Theorem <a href="#n4:thm:weak" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:thm:weak">49</a>.
  - Explanation: Transfers the prepared numerical theorem through fixed-radius strictification, rest replacement and designated-end truncation.
- **claim-four-dimensional-momentum-existence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n4-lem-momentum-exists)): On a smooth four-dimensional asymptotically flat end, suppose $g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q})$ and $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$ for some $q>1$. If $\|J\|_g$ is integrable, where $J_i=\nabla^j(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij})$, then each ADM momentum limit in <a href="#n4:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:intro:momentum">[n4:intro:momentum]</a> exists and is finite.
  - Explanation: Derives existence and finiteness of ADM momentum from the differentiated decay and integrable momentum density.
- **claim-maximal-dec-energy-bound** (theorem, [source](#stmt-n4-ass-energy)): Let $(X^4,g_X,K_X)$ be smooth and connected, with $X$ orientable, $g_X$ complete as a metric space with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $S_X$ included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat and diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\mathbb R^4$. Let $K_X$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor. Suppose $$\begin{gathered} \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{g_X}K_X=0,\qquad \mu_X=\tfrac12(R_{g_X}-\|K_X\|_{g_X}^2) \ge\|\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_{g_X}K_X\|_{g_X},\\ \mu_X,\|\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_{g_X}K_X\|_{g_X}\in L^1(X,\,\mathrm dV_{g_X}). \end{gathered}$$ Assume for some $q>1$ that $$g_X-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K_X=O_1(r^{-1-q}),$$ and that the ADM energy $E_X$ in <a href="#n4:intro:energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:intro:energy">[n4:intro:energy]</a> is finite. On every component of $S_X$, require $H+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{S_X}K_X\le0$ with the normal into $X$. For the one-ended enclosing-cut infimum of Definition <a href="#n4:def:cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:def:cuts">48</a>, denoted here by $a_{g_X}(S_X)$, one has $$E_X\ge\frac12\left(\frac{a_{g_X}(S_X)}{2\pi^2}\right)^{2/3}.$$ The boundary may have any topology and finitely many components. No symmetry, vacuum, spin, outermostness, outer area-minimization or momentum-flux assumption is imposed.
  - Explanation: Deduces the maximal-data energy bound without imposing a momentum-flux existence assumption or additional symmetry and horizon conditions.

There are prepared data $(g_j,K_j)$ on the same exterior, with one fixed $\\beta\\in(0,1)$, numbers $\\epsilon_j\\downarrow0$, and proper diffeomorphisms $\\Phi_j:\\Omega\\longrightarrow\\Omega$ equal to the identity near $S$, such that $$\\label{eq:end:reduction-limits}\n P_j=0,\\qquad E_j\\longrightarrow m,\\qquad\n \\Phi_j^*g\\le(1+\\epsilon_j)g_j,\\qquad\n A_{\\min}^{g_j}(S)\\ge(1+\\epsilon_j)^{-k/2}a.$$ The positive constant $c_j$ in Equation <a href=\"#eq:end:prepared\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:end:prepared\">[eq:end:prepared]</a> and the end coordinates may depend on $j$.",
      "explanation": "Replaces the end by prepared rest data whose energies approach invariant mass and whose enclosing areas retain a lower comparison with the original infimum.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-end-compact-inverses",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal A\\subset\\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected Euclidean annulus and fix a compact subset of its interior. Smooth scalar sources supported in that subset with zero constant and first moments have smooth symmetric solutions of $\\mathsf S(h)=f$ supported in a larger fixed compact subset of $\\mathcal A$. Smooth vector sources with zero integrals against every Euclidean Killing field have similarly supported symmetric solutions of $\\mathsf D(b)=F$. For $1<a<\\infty$ and integers $d\\ge0$, these solutions may be chosen linearly with estimates $$\\|h\\|_{W^{d+2,a}}\\le C_{d,a}\\|f\\|_{W^{d,a}},\\qquad\n \\|b\\|_{W^{d+1,a}}\\le C_{d,a}\\|F\\|_{W^{d,a}}.$$ For arbitrary sources the same conclusions hold after subtracting fixed smooth moment bumps, whose coefficients are bounded by the absolute values of the respective moments.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-end-moments",
        "exact_quote": "Let $h=g-\\delta$, $h^{\\mathrm b}=g^{\\mathrm b}-\\delta$, and $b=K$, $b^{\\mathrm b}=K^{\\mathrm b}$ on their common coordinate tail. Put $H=h-h^{\\mathrm b}$ and $B=b-b^{\\mathrm b}$. Define the scalar and vector commutators on $\\mathcal A_L$ by $$C_L=\\mathsf S(\\chi_LH)-\\chi_L\\mathsf S(H),\\qquad\n F_L=\\mathsf D(\\chi_LB)-\\chi_L\\mathsf D(B),$$ and their rescaled versions on $\\mathcal A$ by $$\\widehat C_L(z)=L^2C_L(Lz),\\qquad\n \\widehat F_L(z)=L^2F_L(Lz).$$ The flat sources $\\mathsf S(H)$ and $\\mathsf D(B)$ are integrable. For every fixed affine scalar function $a(z)$ and every fixed Euclidean Killing field $Y(z)$, $$\\int_{\\mathcal A}a\\widehat C_L\\,dz=o(L^{2-n}),\\qquad\n \\int_{\\mathcal A}Y^i\\widehat F_{L,i}\\,dz=o(L^{2-n}).$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.9"

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-end-strict",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\Omega$ be a smooth connected exterior, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$ included, and with exactly one Euclidean coordinate end outside a compact set. Let $(g,K)$ be smooth up to $S$, with $g-\\delta=O_6(r^{-q})$ and $K=O_5(r^{-1-q})$ for some $q>(n-2)/2$. Choose $0<\\beta<\\min(1,q)$ and a smooth nonnegative function $B\\ge|K|_g$ with $B=O_5(r^{-1-q})$. Then the problem $$\\label{eq:end:strict-pde}\n -\\Delta_g\\phi\n =B\\sqrt{|d\\phi|_g^2+\\varrho^{-2k}}+\\varrho^{-n-\\beta},\n \\qquad \\partial_\\nu\\phi=-1\\text{ on }S,\n \\qquad \\phi\\longrightarrow0\\text{ at infinity}$$ has a smooth positive solution, unique among decaying smooth solutions. It satisfies $$\\label{eq:end:strict-estimates}\n\\begin{gathered}\n \\phi=O_6(r^{2-n}),\\qquad\n \\frac{-\\Delta_g\\phi}{r^{-n-\\beta}}\\longrightarrow1,\\\\\n \\mathfrak f_\\phi:=\\lim_{R\\to\\infty}\n          \\int_{S_R}\\partial_{\\nu_g}\\phi\\,dA_g\\\\\n =-\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_g(S)-\\int_\\Omega\n       \\bigl(B\\sqrt{|d\\phi|^2+\\varrho^{-2k}}\n                    +\\varrho^{-n-\\beta}\\bigr)\\,dV_g<0.\n\\end{gathered}$$ If $K$ is compactly supported, $B$ may be chosen compactly supported. If in addition $g-\\delta=O_d(r^{2-n})$ for all $d$, the solution has this decay through every derivative order.*\n\n\n*Suppose also that the ADM limits of $(g,K)$ exist and are finite, that the data satisfy DEC, and that $\\theta_+(S)\\le0$ on every boundary component. For all sufficiently small $\\delta>0$, $$g_\\delta=e^{2\\delta\\phi}g,\\qquad\n K_\\delta=e^{\\delta\\phi}K$$ satisfy $$\\label{eq:end:strict-margin}\n \\mu_\\delta-|J_\\delta|_{g_\\delta}\\ge c_\\delta\\varrho^{-n-\\beta},\n \\qquad \\theta_{+,\\delta}<0,\n \\qquad E_\\delta=E-\\frac{\\delta}{\\omega}\\mathfrak f_\\phi,\n \\qquad P_\\delta=P.$$ Here $g_\\delta\\ge g$, and their ratio tends uniformly to one as $\\delta\\downarrow0$.",

      },

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-scalar-identity",
        "exact_quote": "For every smooth $f,Z$ and every smooth $g,K$ the following identity holds, without a field equation or energy hypothesis: $$\\frac12e^{2t}R_{\\widehat g}\n =\\mu+J(w)+\\mathcal T+w(F)-F\\tau-u^{-1}\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g V,\n \\label{eq:scalar:identity}$$ where $2\\mu=R_g+\\tau^2-|K|^2$, $J=\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_gP_K$, and $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathcal T={}&\\frac12|T^0|^2+|M+s_pa_wy|^2\n       +\\left(ks_p-\\frac{(k-1)^2}{4}v\\right)|y|^2+ks_pd x^2\\\\\n &-\\frac{k-1}{2k}(F-\\chi j)^2+\\chi j^2-\\chi Fj+F^2\n       +2s_p\\chi j a_w x .\n \\end{aligned}\n \\label{eq:scalar:quadratic}$$ The quantity $\\mathcal T$ is smooth, including where $df=0$.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-thm-elliptic-filled",
        "exact_quote": "Fix smooth prepared data satisfying Equation <a href=\"#eq:end:prepared\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:end:prepared\">[eq:end:prepared]</a> on a complete one-ended exterior with nonempty compact smooth boundary. In particular, $K$ is compactly supported, $g-\\delta=O_d(r^{2-n})$ for every fixed $d$, $R_g=O(r^{-n-\\beta})$ for some $0<\\beta<1$, the dominant-energy margin is bounded below by a positive multiple of $\\varrho^{-n-\\beta}$, and every boundary component is strictly future trapped. Fix $0<\\epsilon<1$ and $$\\frac n4<b_1<\\min\\{n-2,n/2\\}.$$ Use the filled manifolds $\\mathcal M_N$, weights $\\rho_0,\\rho_1,\\rho$, and definitions in Equation <a href=\"#eq:scalar:variables\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:scalar:variables\">[eq:scalar:variables]</a>. Choose $\\delta_0>0$ and the polynomial $C_N$ as in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:scalar:floor\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:scalar:floor\">17</a>. For all sufficiently large integers $N>k=n-1$, there are smooth functions $f,Z$ on $\\mathcal M_N$ solving Equation <a href=\"#eq:scalar:system\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:scalar:system\">[eq:scalar:system]</a>. The associated function $t$ satisfies $$\\label{eq:elliptic:polynomial-bounds}\n -\\epsilon<t\\le Z\\le P(N),\\qquad\n \\ell\\le l(t)\\le e,\\qquad\n |f|+|df|_g\\le \\exp(P(N)),\\qquad \\ell=e^{-N\\epsilon}.$$ Here and below $P$ is a polynomial with coefficients depending only on the fixed prepared data, $n$, $\\epsilon$, and the fixed choices in the filling. The height $h=\\eta f$, $\\eta=\\ell^{3/2}$, obeys $$\\label{eq:elliptic:height-bound}\n |h|\\le C,\\qquad |h(x)|\\le C r(x)^{-b_1}\n \\quad\\hbox{on the original end},$$ where $C$ is independent of $N$. At each fixed $N$, for every integer $j\\ge0$ there are constants $C_{N,j}$ and $a_N>0$ such that on that end $$\\label{eq:elliptic:end-bounds}\n |D^j f|\\le C_{N,j}e^{-a_Nr},\\qquad\n t,Z=O_j(r^{2-n}),\\qquad\n \\Delta_g t=O(r^{-n-\\beta}).$$ The constants in Equation <a href=\"#eq:elliptic:end-bounds\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:elliptic:end-bounds\">[eq:elliptic:end-bounds]</a>, and higher derivative bounds on compact sets, may depend arbitrarily on fixed $N$.",

      },

The height $h=\\eta f$, $\\eta=\\ell^{3/2}$, obeys $$\\label{eq:elliptic:height-bound}\n |h|\\le C,\\qquad |h(x)|\\le C r(x)^{-b_1}\n \\quad\\hbox{on the original end},$$ where $C$ is independent of $N$. Use $p(t)=N\\vartheta(Nt)$ and $l(t)=\\exp(\\int_0^t p(s)\\,ds)$, with the smooth cutoff $\\vartheta$ of Equation <a href=\"#eq:scalar:parameters\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:scalar:parameters\">[eq:scalar:parameters]</a>, and define $D$, $t$, $A_\\chi$ by Equations <a href=\"#eq:scalar:implicit\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:scalar:implicit\">[eq:scalar:implicit]</a> and <a href=\"#eq:scalar:variables\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:scalar:variables\">[eq:scalar:variables]</a>. Put $K_a=aK$. The solution map is continuous from $[0,1]\\times C^{1,\\gamma}(\\mathcal D)$ to $C^{3,\\gamma}(\\mathcal D)$ and maps bounded sets to bounded sets.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-n3-reduction-conformal-formulas",
        "exact_quote": "For a smooth function $f$, set $$g_f=e^{4f}g,\\qquad K_f=e^{2f}K.$$ The corresponding constraint densities satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n 16\\pi e^{4f}\\mu_f\n   &=16\\pi\\mu-8\\Delta_g f-8|df|_g^2,\n       \\label{n3:reduction:conformal-energy}\\\\\n 8\\pi J_f\n   &=e^{-2f}\\bigl(8\\pi J+4K(\\nabla f,\\cdot)\\bigr).\n       \\label{n3:reduction:conformal-momentum}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here the second identity is an identity of covectors. Consequently, $$\\begin{aligned}\n 16\\pi e^{4f}(\\mu_f-|J_f|_{g_f})\n \\ge{}&16\\pi(\\mu-|J|_g)\\notag\\\\\n &+8\\bigl(-\\Delta_g f-|df|_g^2-|K|_g|df|_g\\bigr).\n       \\label{n3:reduction:conformal-dec}\n\\end{aligned}$$ On the fixed boundary, $$\\theta_{+,f}=e^{-2f}(\\theta_++4\\partial_\\nu f).\n       \\label{n3:reduction:conformal-expansion}$$ Equivalently, if $u=e^f>0$, the last summand in Equation <a href=\"#n3:reduction:conformal-dec\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:reduction:conformal-dec\">[n3:reduction:conformal-dec]</a> is $8u^{-1}(-\\Delta_g u-|K|_g|du|_g)$.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.9"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-n3-reduction-strict-direction",
        "exact_quote": "Choose $$0<\\delta<\\beta<\\min(q,1).$$ There are smooth positive functions $w$ and $\\phi$ on $\\Omega$, with $w=r^{-3-\\delta}$ on the end, such that $$\\begin{aligned}\n &\\partial_\\nu\\phi=-1\\quad\\hbox{on }B,\n       &\\phi&=O_2(r^{-1}),\\label{n3:reduction:strict-boundary}\\\\\n &-\\Delta_g\\phi-|K|_g|d\\phi|_g\\ge w,\n       &\\frac{-\\Delta_g\\phi}{w}&\\longrightarrow1.\n       \\label{n3:reduction:strict-source}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The Euclidean normal flux $$L_\\phi=\\lim_{r\\to\\infty}\n          \\int_{S_r}\\partial_r\\phi\\,\\,\\mathrm dA_\\delta$$ is finite and negative. For every finite $s\\ge0$, set $$\\label{n3:reduction:linear-family}\n u_s=1+s\\phi,\\qquad g_s=u_s^4g,\\qquad K_s=u_s^2K.$$ These data are complete up to $B$ and satisfy DEC, strictly for $s>0$. If $\\theta_+\\le0$ on $B$, their boundary expansion remains nonpositive and is strictly negative for $s>0$. Their decay exponent can be taken to be $\\min(q,1)>1/2$, their constraint densities are integrable, and $$\\label{n3:reduction:strict-charges}\n E_s=E+sA_\\phi,\\qquad P_s=P,\n \\qquad A_\\phi=-\\frac{L_\\phi}{2\\pi}>0.$$ Their full enclosing infima satisfy $$\\label{n3:reduction:strict-areas}\n a_g(B)\\le a_{g_s}(B)\n       \\le (1+s\\|\\phi\\|_\\infty)^4a_g(B).$$ In particular $E_s\\to E$ and $a_{g_s}(B)\\to a_g(B)$ as $s\\downarrow0$. No sign assumption on the ADM vector is needed.*\n\n*If $K$ is compactly supported and the metric has symbol estimates of all orders with $g-\\delta=O(r^{-1})$, the function can instead be chosen with $\\phi=O_k(r^{-1})$ for every $k$, while retaining Equations <a href=\"#n3:reduction:strict-boundary\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:reduction:strict-boundary\">[n3:reduction:strict-boundary]</a> and <a href=\"#n3:reduction:strict-source\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:reduction:strict-source\">[n3:reduction:strict-source]</a>.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.9"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-n3-reduction-area-compactness",
        "exact_quote": "Let $g_j$ be smooth metrics on the fixed exterior $\\Omega$, converging to $g$ locally uniformly up to $B$. Suppose that in a fixed chart outside a compact set they satisfy, with constants independent of $j$, $$\\label{n3:reduction:area-geometry}\n c\\delta\\le g_j\\le C\\delta,\\qquad r|\\partial g_j|_\\delta\\le C.$$ Suppose also that each $g_j$ has an asymptotically flat end, possibly in a different chart, and admits a fixed compact enclosing competitor with uniformly bounded area. Then minimizing filled enclosures exist, their boundaries lie in one fixed compact subset of $\\Omega$, and $$a_{g_j}(B)\\longrightarrow a_g(B).$$ The perimeter and smooth enclosing infima agree.         "exact_quote": "The data in Proposition <a href=\"#n3:reduction:annular-replacement\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:reduction:annular-replacement\">41</a> can be modified farther out, inside their exact Schwarzschild part, so that they are induced by a constant-static-time slice outside a compact set.         "anchor": "stmt-n3-reduction-rest-reduction",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(\\Omega,g,K)$ satisfy the exterior hypotheses of Theorem <a href=\"#n3:intro:exterior-inequality\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:intro:exterior-inequality\">33</a>, including $\\theta_+\\le0$ on its smooth compact boundary, and let $m=(E^2-|P|^2)^{1/2}>0$. There is a sequence of smooth exterior data $(g_j,K_j)$ on $\\Omega$ with the following properties:*\n\n1.  *$\\mu_j>|J_j|_{g_j}$ everywhere and $\\theta_{+,j}<0$ on $B$. The constraint densities are integrable. On the end their DEC margin is bounded below by $c_jr^{-3-\\delta}$ for some $c_j>0$ and one fixed $0<\\delta<1$. For a smooth positive radius extension $\\rho$, the constant can be decreased so that $\\mu_j-|J_j|_{g_j}\\ge c_j\\rho^{-3-\\delta}$ on all of $\\Omega$.*\n\n2.  *$K_j$ is compactly supported, and in a rest chart $g_j-\\delta=O_k(r^{-1})$ and $R_{g_j}=O_k(r^{-3-\\delta})$ for every $k$. In particular $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_{g_j}=O(r^{-3})$ there. Their ADM momentum is zero.*\n\n3.  *$(g_j,K_j)\\to(g,K)$ smoothly on every fixed compact subset up to the boundary, their ADM energies satisfy $E_j\\to m$, and $a_{g_j}(B)\\to a_g(B)$.*\n\n*Consequently it suffices to prove the energy/enclosing-area inequality for the class in <span class=\"upright\">(i)</span>–<span class=\"upright\">(ii)</span> in order to prove Theorem <a href=\"#n3:intro:exterior-inequality\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n3:intro:exterior-inequality\">33</a> in its stated class.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-bridge-intro-global-penrose",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(M,g,K)$ be a connected orientable smooth three-dimensional initial data set without boundary, with $g$ complete. Suppose that outside a compact set $M$ has finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end, in its asymptotic coordinates, assume $$g-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\\qquad q>\\tfrac12,$$ and finite ADM energy and momentum limits with the normalizations <a href=\"#n3:intro:energy\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:intro:energy\">[n3:intro:energy]</a>–<a href=\"#n3:intro:momentum\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:intro:momentum\">[n3:intro:momentum]</a>. The decay exponents may differ between ends. Assume that the physical constraint densities <a href=\"#n3:intro:constraints\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:intro:constraints\">[n3:intro:constraints]</a> obey $\\mu\\ge|J|_g$ and that both $\\mu$ and $|J|_g$ are integrable on $M$.*\n\n*For every chosen end and every admissible boundary $S$ in Definition <a href=\"#bridge:intro:global-admissible\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"bridge:intro:global-admissible\">46</a>, its ADM vector $(E,P)$ satisfies $$\\label{bridge:intro:global-inequality}\n E>|P|_\\delta,\\qquad\n \\sqrt{E^2-|P|_\\delta^2}\\ge\n                         \\sqrt{\\frac{A_{\\min}(S)}{16\\pi}}.$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.9"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-n4-thm-weak",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(M^4,g,K)$ be smooth and connected, with $M$ orientable, $K$ an arbitrary smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $S=\\partial M$ nonempty, compact, and smooth. Suppose $g$ is complete as a metric space with $S$ included. Outside a compact set let $M$ have finitely many, and at least one, ends diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\\mathbb R^4$. Assume $$\\mu\\ge|J|_g,\\qquad \\mu,|J|_g\\in L^1(M,\\,\\mathrm dV_g),$$ and, on every end for a common $q>1$, $$g-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),$$ with finite energy and momentum limits <a href=\"#n4:intro:energy\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n4:intro:energy\">[n4:intro:energy]</a>–<a href=\"#n4:intro:momentum\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n4:intro:momentum\">[n4:intro:momentum]</a>. On every component of $S$ assume $\\Theta_K\\le0$, with normal into $M$.*\n\n\n*Then for each end $e$, $$\\label{n4:intro:main}\n E_e\\ge\n \\sqrt{|P_e|_\\delta^2+\n       \\frac14\\left(\\frac{A_e(S)}{\\omega_3}\\right)^{4/3}}.$$ In particular $E_e>|P_e|_\\delta$, and the invariant mass satisfies $$\\label{n4:intro:mass}\n \\sqrt{E_e^2-|P_e|_\\delta^2}\n   \\ge\\frac12\\left(\\frac{A_e(S)}{\\omega_3}\\right)^{2/3}.$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.9"
      },
      "evidence": [

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-n4-lem-cut-reduction",
        "exact_quote": "Under the hypotheses of Theorem <a href=\"#n4:thm:weak\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"n4:thm:weak\">49</a>, the quantity $A_e(S)$ is finite and strictly positive for every end $e$. Truncating all other ends at sufficiently large coordinate spheres gives a connected, complete one-ended exterior $M_T$ with compact smooth boundary $S_T$. All its boundary components have future nonpositive expansion with the normal into $M_T$. Its selected-end charges are the original charges, and $$\\label{n4:end:cut-truncation}\n A_*(M_T,g)\\ge A_e(S),\\qquad\n \\lim_{T\\to\\infty}A_*(M_T,g)=A_e(S).$$ The common parameter $T$ in the limit can be replaced by any exhaustion in which every unwanted truncation radius tends to infinity.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.9"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-n4-lem-conformal",
        "exact_quote": "Let $u>0$ be smooth, and set $g_u=u^2g$, $K_u=uK$. In dimension four, as an identity of scalar functions and an identity of covectors, respectively, $$\\begin{aligned}\n u^2\\mu_u&=\\mu-3u^{-1}\\Delta_g u,\\label{n4:end:conformal-mu}\\\\\n uJ_u&=J+3K(\\mathop{\\mathrm{grad}}_g\\log u,\\cdot).\\label{n4:end:conformal-J}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Consequently, $$\\label{n4:end:conformal-dec}\n u^2\\bigl(\\mu_u-|J_u|_{g_u}\\bigr)\n \\ge \\mu-|J|_g+3u^{-1}\n          \\bigl(-\\Delta_g u-|K|_g|\\,\\mathrm du|_g\\bigr).$$ For any consistently oriented hypersurface, $$\\label{n4:end:conformal-expansion}\n \\Theta_{K_u}=u^{-1}\n       \\bigl(\\Theta_K+3\\partial_\\nu\\log u\\bigr).$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.9"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {

          "source_id": "PM-260.9"

      "conclusion": {

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-n4-lem-strictification",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected four-dimensional exterior, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary included, with one Euclidean coordinate end and compact complement. Suppose $\\mu\\ge |J|_g$ and $\\Theta_K\\le0$ on every boundary component, where the boundary normal $\\nu$ points into $M$. Assume that $K$ has compact support and that, outside a compact set, $$g=\\left(1+\\frac{c}{r^2}\\right)^2\\delta$$ in the end coordinates, for a constant $c$. Fix $0<\\delta_1<1$, and extend the coordinate radius to a positive smooth function $r$ on $M$.*\n\n*There is a nonnegative smooth function $\\phi$, with $\\phi=O_k(r^{-2})$ for every fixed derivative order $k$, such that, for all sufficiently small $s>0$, the data $$(g_s,K_s)=(e^{2s\\phi}g,e^{s\\phi}K)$$ satisfy $$\\label{n4:eq:strictification-output}\n \\Theta_{K_s}<0,\\qquad\n \\mu_s-|J_s|_{g_s}\\ge c_s r^{-4-\\delta_1}\n \\quad\\hbox{on }M,\\qquad c_s>0.$$ They are complete, have compactly supported second fundamental form, integrable constraint densities, zero ADM momentum and finite ADM energy. Their end satisfies $$\\label{n4:eq:strictification-decay}\n g_s-\\delta=O_k(r^{-2})\\quad\\hbox{for every fixed }k,\n \\qquad R_{g_s}=O(r^{-4-\\delta_1}).$$ For the full enclosing-cut infimum on this fixed exterior, $$\\label{n4:eq:strictification-limits}\n E_{g_s}\\longrightarrow E_g,\n \\qquad A_*(g_s)\\longrightarrow A_*(g)\n \\quad\\hbox{as }s\\downarrow0.$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.9"
      },

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-n4-ass-energy",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"n4:cor:maximal-dec\" label=\"n4:cor:maximal-dec\"></span>Let $(X^4,g_X,K_X)$ be smooth and connected, with $X$ orientable, $g_X$ complete as a metric space with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $S_X$ included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat and diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\\mathbb R^4$. Let $K_X$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor. Suppose $$\\begin{gathered}\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{g_X}K_X=0,\\qquad\n \\mu_X=\\tfrac12(R_{g_X}-|K_X|_{g_X}^2)\n       \\ge|\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_{g_X}K_X|_{g_X},\\\\\n \\mu_X,|\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_{g_X}K_X|_{g_X}\\in L^1(X,\\,\\mathrm dV_{g_X}).\n\\end{gathered}$$ Assume for some $q>1$ that $$g_X-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad K_X=O_1(r^{-1-q}),$$ and that the ADM energy $E_X$ in <a href=\"#n4:intro:energy\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n4:intro:energy\">[n4:intro:energy]</a> is finite. On every component of $S_X$, require $H+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{S_X}K_X\\le0$ with the normal into $X$.
