<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Initial-data exterior** ([source](#stmt-def-data)): Let $n\geq3$ and let $\Omega$ be a smooth connected orientable $n$-manifold with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$. The metric $g$ and symmetric covariant two-tensor $K$ are smooth up to $S$, and $g$ is complete with $S$ included. Outside a compact set, $\Omega$ is a single coordinate end $\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|>R_0\}$. Thus there are no additional ends hidden in the compact-complement condition. Write $R_g$ for scalar curvature and $\nabla$ for the connection of $g$. Write $\tau=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK$. Our constraint normalization is $$\label{eq:setting:constraints} 2\mu=R_g+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)^2-\|K\|_g^2,\qquad J_i=\nabla^j\bigl(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\bigr).$$ The dominant energy condition is $\mu\geq\|J\|_g$. We require $\mu,\|J\|_g\in L^1(\Omega,dV_g)$. Along $S$ the unit normal $\nu$ points into $\Omega$, toward the end. Its future expansion is $$\theta_+=H_S+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK,\qquad H_S=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_S\nu,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK=(g^{ij}-\nu^i\nu^j)K_{ij}.$$ The boundary is weakly future trapped when $\theta_+\leq0$ on every component. No condition is imposed on the other null expansion. For coordinate tensors, $T=O_j(r^{-a})$ means $\|\partial^\alpha T\|\leq C_\alpha r^{-a-\|\alpha\|}$ for $\|\alpha\|\leq j$, where $r=\|x\|$. The decay orders will be specified in each theorem. Set $k=n-1$ and $\omega=\omega_{n-1}=\|\mathbb S^{n-1}\|$. The Laplacian is $\Delta=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}\nabla$ and symmetrization includes a factor $1/2$. We require the finite ADM limits $$\begin{aligned} E&=\frac{1}{2(n-1)\omega_{n-1}}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{\|x\|=R}(\partial_jg_{ij}-\partial_i g_{jj}) n_\delta^i\,dA_\delta,\label{eq:setting:energy}\\ P_i&=\frac{1}{(n-1)\omega_{n-1}}\lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{\|x\|=R}\bigl(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\bigr) n_\delta^j\,dA_\delta.\label{eq:setting:momentum} \end{aligned}$$ Here $n_\delta$ and $dA_\delta$ are Euclidean. If $E>\|P\|_\delta$, define $m=(E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2)^{1/2}$.
- **Full enclosing cut and enclosing-area infimum** ([source](#stmt-def-fullcuts)): A *full enclosing cut* is the entire intrinsic manifold boundary $\Gamma=\partial D$ of a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D\subset\Omega$. We require $D$ to be closed in $\Omega$, its manifold interior to lie in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, and $D$ to contain the whole sufficiently distant end. Its full boundary must be compact, smooth, embedded and two-sided. In particular, $D=\Omega$ is admissible and has boundary $S$. Define $$\label{eq:setting:minarea} A_{\min,g}(S)=\inf_D\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(\partial D).$$ The use of intrinsic boundary ensures that coincident portions of $S$ are counted. A cut need not be connected, trapped or minimal. The infimum need not be attained.
- **Prepared exterior** ([source](#stmt-def-prepared)): Let $(\Omega^n,g_0,K_0)$ be a smooth connected orientable one-ended exterior with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$, complete with $S$ included and with compact complement of its Euclidean coordinate end. Use the constraint and ADM conventions of Equations <a href="#eq:setting:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:constraints">[eq:setting:constraints]</a>–<a href="#eq:setting:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:momentum">[eq:setting:momentum]</a>. Let $\varrho$ be a smooth positive function on the closed exterior, equal to the coordinate radius on a distant tail. Require that, for some $0<\beta<1$ and $c>0$, $$\label{eq:end:prepared} \begin{gathered} \operatorname{supp}K_0\text{ is compact},\qquad g_0-\delta=O_d(r^{2-n})\text{ for every fixed }d,\\ R_{g_0}=O(r^{-n-\beta}),\qquad \mu_0-\|J_0\|_{g_0}\ge c\varrho^{-n-\beta},\qquad H_S+\operatorname{tr}_S K_0<0\text{ on every component of }S. \end{gathered}$$ The constraint densities are integrable. The ADM momentum is $P_0=0$; write $E_0$ for the energy. Finally the full-cut infimum, with every component and all contact counted as in Definition <a href="#def:fullcuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:fullcuts">2</a>, is $A_0=A_{\min,g_0}(S)>0$.
- **Three-dimensional exterior and enclosing area** ([source](#stmt-n3-intro-exterior-class)): An exterior is a connected orientable smooth three-manifold $\Omega$ with nonempty compact smooth boundary, complete as a metric space with its boundary included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat. An enclosing cut is the entire compact smooth embedded two-sided intrinsic boundary of a connected closed outer domain containing the sufficiently distant end, with its manifold interior in the open exterior. Equivalently, it separates the entire inner boundary from infinity, with bounded complementary pockets filled on the inner side. Every frontier component is counted, including portions coinciding with the inner boundary. A cut may have several components. Its normal points toward the retained end. We put $$a_g(\partial\Omega)= \inf\{\|\Gamma\|_g:\Gamma\text{ is an enclosing cut}\}.$$ When using perimeter compactness, we take the closure of this class among filled inner sets and include the area of any frontier coinciding with the obstacle. Smooth outward approximation gives the same infimum. Enclosing cuts and minimizing sets are taken with bounded complementary pockets filled. Auxiliary perimeter arguments may use competitors containing the inner obstacle before filling: filling a bounded pocket deletes its frontier, cannot increase perimeter, and leaves the enclosing infimum unchanged.
- **Admissible boundary and ambient enclosing area** ([source](#stmt-bridge-intro-global-admissible)): Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth three-dimensional initial data set without boundary, with $M$ connected, and fix one asymptotically flat end $e$. An admissible boundary for $e$ is a nonempty compact smooth embedded two-sided surface $S=\partial D^+$, where $D^+$ is a smooth open region containing the entire sufficiently distant part of $e$. The surface and the region may be disconnected, and $D^+$ may contain other ends. For the normal $\nu$ pointing into $D^+$, require $$H_S+\operatorname{tr}_S K\le0.$$ Its minimum enclosing area is $$\label{bridge:intro:global-area} A_{\min}(S)=\inf\left\{ \operatorname{Area}_g(\partial D'^+): \begin{array}{l} D'^+\subseteq D^+\text{ is a smooth open region containing}\\ \text{the entire sufficiently distant part of }e,\\ \partial D'^+\text{ is compact, smooth, and embedded} \end{array}\right\}.$$ The full boundary area is counted, including portions coincident with $S$. Competitor regions $D'^+$ may be disconnected and may retain other ends. Their boundaries need be neither trapped nor minimal. The definition imposes no sign condition on the inward null expansion.
- **Four-dimensional end-isolating enclosing cuts** ([source](#stmt-n4-def-cuts)): Let $M$ have nonempty compact boundary $S$ and finitely many asymptotically flat ends, and fix an end $e$. An admissible outer domain $D_e$ is a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold with boundary, closed as a subset of $M$, such that its manifold interior lies in $\operatorname{int}M$, it contains the entire sufficiently distant part of $e$, and it contains no sufficiently distant part of any other end. Its entire intrinsic manifold boundary $\Gamma=\partial_{\mathrm{man}}D_e$ is required to be compact. The enclosing volume is $$A_e(S)=\inf_{D_e}\|\partial_{\mathrm{man}}D_e\|_g.$$ All frontier coincident with $S$ is counted. The cut may be disconnected. In the one-ended case $D_e=M$ is allowed and has intrinsic boundary $S$. We then also write $A_*$ for this infimum.
- **Implicit conformal variable** ([source](#eq:scalar:implicit)): For smooth unknowns $f,Z$, define $t$ implicitly by $$Z=t+\frac{1}{2k}\log D,\qquad D=1+l(t)^2\|df\|_g^2. \label{eq:scalar:implicit}$$
- **Graph, trace and divergence variables** ([source](#eq:scalar:variables)): Use $g$ to identify vectors and covectors and set $$\begin{aligned} &w=lD^{-1/2}\nabla f,\qquad a_w=\|w\|,\qquad v=a_w^2,\qquad d=D^{-1}=1-v,\\ &\chi=\frac{kd}{k+pv},\qquad A_d=I-w\otimes w,\qquad A_\chi=I-\frac{k+p}{k+pv}w\otimes w,\\ &H^f=lD^{-1/2}\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_g f,\qquad L=K+H^f,\qquad F=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{A_\chi}L,\qquad h=\eta f,\\ &U=l\sqrt D,\qquad u=e^{(k-1)t}U,\qquad V=uA_\chi\bigl(k\nabla Z+K(w,\cdot)\bigr),\\ &\bar g=g+l^2df\otimes df,\qquad \widehat g=e^{2t}\bar g, \qquad s_p=p+\frac{k-1}{2}. \end{aligned} \label{eq:scalar:variables}$$
- **Full perimeter and reduced boundary** ([source](#pm-h-34)): For a measurable set $F$ and an open set $U$, write $P_\gamma(F;U)=\|D\mathbf1_F\|_\gamma(U)$ for perimeter in a smooth metric $\gamma$, and $P_\gamma(F)=P_\gamma(F;\mathcal M_N)$.
- **Dominant energy condition** ([source](#eq:setting:constraints)): The dominant energy condition is $\mu\geq\|J\|_g$.
- **Weak future trapping** ([source](#eq:setting:constraints)): The boundary is weakly future trapped when $\theta_+\leq0$ on every component.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-boost-reference-charges** [claim](#stmt-lem-end-boost) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-end-boost): Compute the homogeneous ADM fluxes and their ellipsoid angular integral. -> Charge-matched reference end and differentiated remainders.
- **step-compact-linear-inverses** [claim](#stmt-lem-end-compact-inverses) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-end-compact-inverses): Iterate compact divergence inversion, correct skew stress and remove moment obstructions with dual bumps. -> Compact symmetric constraint corrections with Sobolev derivative gains.
- **step-sublinear-moment-control** [claim](#stmt-lem-end-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-end-moments): Use integrable flat sources, charge matching and Green flux identities before rescaling. -> Small rescaled compatibility moments.
- **step-strong-strictification** [claim](#stmt-lem-end-strict) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-end-strict): Continue mixed-boundary scalar problems, obtain truncation-independent barriers, exhaust and compute the conformal charge change. -> Positive decaying strictification function and strict DEC and trapping margins.
- **step-strong-rest-preparation** [claim](#stmt-prop-end-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-end-strict-2): Join to the boosted end, bend inside vacuum, repair the deficit, compare every cut by proper compression, then strictify each fixed replacement. -> Prepared rest data with invariant-mass energy limit and area lower comparison.
- **step-strong-positive-shell** [claim](#stmt-lem-end-positive-shell) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-end-positive-shell): Switch a radial superharmonic tail smoothly to a constant on the core and compute its exact ADM energy increment. -> Energy-raising family with fixed momentum and nondecreasing full-cut areas.
- **step-exact-scalar-identity** [claim](#stmt-prop-scalar-identity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-scalar-identity): Combine stationary Lorentz curvature, graph geometry and conformal scalar curvature, then redistribute the weighted divergence. -> Smooth invariant scalar identity including cutoff derivative contributions.
- **step-weighted-coercivity** [claim](#stmt-prop-scalar-coercivity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-scalar-coercivity): Complete the axial squares and retain the axial weights when recovering the original blocks. -> Nonnegative quadratic form and polynomial weighted coercivity.
- **step-uniform-height-comparison** [claim](#stmt-lem-elliptic-height) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-elliptic-height): Apply extrema tests and radial barriers to the trace equation, then estimate the outer normal derivative. -> Uniform normalized-height bounds and outer-floor exclusion.
- **step-pointwise-floor-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-lem-scalar-floor) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-scalar-floor): Compare scalar curvature at a minimum with the penalized divergence source and choose the penalty polynomial to force a contradiction. -> No above-domain fixed point reaches the floor in the interior.
- **step-polynomial-potential-upper-bound** [claim](#stmt-prop-elliptic-upper) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-elliptic-upper): Control high-level weighted mass, derive a product-graph Sobolev inequality and close exponential iteration. -> Polynomial potential bound and fixed-parameter uniform ellipticity.
- **step-rankone-gradient-estimate** [claim](#stmt-lem-elliptic-gradient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-elliptic-gradient): Combine strict Hessian absorption, trace-reversed flux, gradient-norm drop and frozen-axis affine improvement, including the reflected boundary flux correction. -> Gradient continuity and Hessian mass decay; the printed statement contains an incomplete gradient-norm expression.
- **step-natural-growth-oscillation** [claim](#stmt-lem-elliptic-natural-growth) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-elliptic-natural-growth): Reflect constant Dirichlet data, absorb quadratic growth with both exponential signs and estimate source potentials to reduce oscillation. -> Uniform scalar Hölder bound without a coefficient continuity modulus.
- **step-coupled-regularity-bootstrap** [claim](#stmt-prop-elliptic-regularity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-elliptic-regularity): Apply trace regularity before divergence regularity, then use scalar Schauder estimates and local absorption of quadratic gradient growth. -> Every fixed derivative bound uniform in outer truncation at fixed deformation parameter.
- **step-arbitrary-trial-trace-map** [claim](#stmt-lem-elliptic-trial-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-elliptic-trial-trace): Continue the scalar trace problem using logarithmic boundary and paired-point barriers, then prove uniqueness and continuous dependence. -> Trace solution map defined without a floor restriction.
- **step-filled-global-solvability** [claim](#stmt-thm-elliptic-filled) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-elliptic-trial-trace-2): Use the compact trial map and moving-domain degree homotopies, exhaust outer radii at fixed deformation parameter, then prove exponential graph decay and potential decay. -> Smooth global filled solution and differentiated end estimates.
- **step-penalty-flux-bound** [claim](#stmt-prop-scalar-flux) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-scalar-flux): Integrate on the smooth filled manifold, normalize the conformal ADM flux and absorb penalty-band gradient terms by the favorable source. -> Energy upper error controlled by a polynomial times decaying scales.
- **step-negative-filling-height** [claim](#stmt-lem-height-ramp) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-height-ramp): Build cap and collar supersolutions with a controlled neck ramp and apply the trace maximum test. -> Uniform negative height on the entire filling and near the boundary.
- **step-small-height-scalar-curvature** [claim](#stmt-lem-height-curvature) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-height-curvature): Apply a height-dependent conformal plateau and absorb its derivative errors with the strict energy margin and weighted squares. -> Nonnegative exterior scalar curvature, metric domination and unchanged asymptotic energy under the plateau.
- **step-obstacle-minimizer-existence** [claim](#stmt-lem-height-bv-existence) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-height-bv-existence): Clip competitors with mean-convex distant spheres, use BV compactness and lower semicontinuity, then maximize volume among minimizers. -> Maximal bounded perimeter minimizer with exponential-polynomial perimeter bound.
- **step-two-density-detachment** [claim](#stmt-lem-height-detachment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-height-detachment): Obtain the filled density from the distance collar and the unfilled density from ball-filling minimality, then contradict the competitor bound using plateau area inflation. -> Frontier separated from the obstacle.
- **step-prepared-geometric-output** [claim](#stmt-prop-height-enclosure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-height-detachment-2): Use minimizing-boundary regularity, eliminate bounded complementary pockets, approximate by full original cuts and verify intrinsic completeness and end decay. -> Connected Riemannian exterior meeting all receiving hypotheses of the minimizing-frontier inequality.
- **step-prepared-numerical-comparison** [claim](#stmt-thm-numerical-prepared) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-numerical-prepared): Apply the quoted Riemannian inequality to each actual exterior, then take numerical limits in the prescribed order. -> Prepared energy inequality.
- **step-main-inequality-and-sharpness** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-numerical-prepared-2): Apply the prepared bound to each fixed replacement and pass its charge and area comparisons to the limit; use radial calibration on the static equality model. -> Sharp original-data invariant-mass bound.
- **step-strong-automatic-timelikeness** [claim](#stmt-cor-automatic-timelikeness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-numerical-prepared-3): Approach the future null cone through positive-shell data while retaining a fixed positive enclosing-area lower bound. -> Strict future timelikeness and the inequality for the original datum.
- **step-three-dimensional-positive-area** [claim](#stmt-bridge-bridge-positive-area) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bridge-bridge-positive-area): Carry a closed bounded-comass form along a proper tube and use Stokes' theorem on every full cut, with collar approximation for boundary coincidence. -> Finite positive enclosing-area infimum.
- **step-three-dimensional-conformal-laws** [claim](#stmt-n3-reduction-conformal-formulas) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-reduction-conformal-formulas): Specialize the general conformal formulas while converting geometric densities to physical densities. -> Physical constraint and expansion transformation identities.
- **step-three-dimensional-strict-family** [claim](#stmt-n3-reduction-strict-direction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-reduction-strict-direction): Solve a regularized mixed-boundary drift problem by continuation and exhaustion, then use a linear positive conformal factor and compute its flux. -> Strict family with positive energy slope, fixed momentum and enclosing-area comparison.
- **step-three-dimensional-area-compactness** [claim](#stmt-n3-reduction-area-compactness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-reduction-area-compactness): Construct perimeter minimizers, use distant-ball density to confine their frontiers and combine BV compactness with local uniform metric convergence. -> Full convergence of enclosing infima and smooth/perimeter equivalence.
- **step-three-dimensional-reference-plane** [claim](#stmt-n3-reduction-boosted-reference) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-reduction-boosted-reference): Specialize the boosted reference charge calculation and check the physical ADM normalization. -> Reference plane with exactly matching charges.
- **step-three-dimensional-compact-corrections** [claim](#stmt-n3-reduction-compact-inverses) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-reduction-compact-inverses): Specialize the annular scalar and symmetric-divergence inverses and their trace reversal. -> Compact corrections with the required Sobolev estimates.
- **step-three-dimensional-first-moments** [claim](#stmt-n3-reduction-moment-estimates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-n3-reduction-moment-estimates): Expand the physical constraints around Euclidean data and control weighted tail integrals by integrability. -> Integrable linear sources and sublinear first boundary moments.

          "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathcal D$ be a compact smooth $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth boundary, with $n\\ge3$ and $k=n-1$, and let $K$ be a smooth symmetric tensor on $\\mathcal D$.       "claim_anchor": "stmt-n3-reduction-conformal-formulas",

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-n3-reduction-conformal-formulas",
          "exact_quote": "For a smooth function $f$, set $$g_f=e^{4f}g,\\qquad K_f=e^{2f}K.$$ The corresponding constraint densities satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n 16\\pi e^{4f}\\mu_f\n   &=16\\pi\\mu-8\\Delta_g f-8|df|_g^2,\n       \\label{n3:reduction:conformal-energy}\\\\\n 8\\pi J_f\n   &=e^{-2f}\\bigl(8\\pi J+4K(\\nabla f,\\cdot)\\bigr).\n       \\label{n3:reduction:conformal-momentum}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here the second identity is an identity of covectors. Consequently, $$\\begin{aligned}\n 16\\pi e^{4f}(\\mu_f-|J_f|_{g_f})\n \\ge{}&16\\pi(\\mu-|J|_g)\\notag\\\\\n &+8\\bigl(-\\Delta_g f-|df|_g^2-|K|_g|df|_g\\bigr).\n       \\label{n3:reduction:conformal-dec}\n\\end{aligned}$$ On the fixed boundary, $$\\theta_{+,f}=e^{-2f}(\\theta_++4\\partial_\\nu f).\n       \\label{n3:reduction:conformal-expansion}$$ Equivalently, if $u=e^f>0$, the last summand in Equation <a href=\"#n3:reduction:conformal-dec\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:reduction:conformal-dec\">[n3:reduction:conformal-dec]</a> is $8u^{-1}(-\\Delta_g u-|K|_g|du|_g)$.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.9"
        }
      ],
      "id": "step-three-dimensional-conformal-laws",
      "inputs": [
        "Smooth conformal function",
        "Fixed future-normal convention"
      ],
      "method": "Specialize the general conformal formulas while converting geometric densities to physical densities.",
      "output": "Physical constraint and expansion transformation identities.",
      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-n3-reduction-conformal-formulas"
    },

        {
          "anchor": "stmt-n3-reduction-strict-direction",
          "exact_quote": "Choose $$0<\\delta<\\beta<\\min(q,1).$$ There are smooth positive functions $w$ and $\\phi$ on $\\Omega$, with $w=r^{-3-\\delta}$ on the end, such that $$\\begin{aligned}\n &\\partial_\\nu\\phi=-1\\quad\\hbox{on }B,\n       &\\phi&=O_2(r^{-1}),\\label{n3:reduction:strict-boundary}\\\\\n &-\\Delta_g\\phi-|K|_g|d\\phi|_g\\ge w,\n       &\\frac{-\\Delta_g\\phi}{w}&\\longrightarrow1.\n       \\label{n3:reduction:strict-source}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The Euclidean normal flux $$L_\\phi=\\lim_{r\\to\\infty}\n          \\int_{S_r}\\partial_r\\phi\\,\\,\\mathrm dA_\\delta$$ is finite and negative. For every finite $s\\ge0$, set $$\\label{n3:reduction:linear-family}\n u_s=1+s\\phi,\\qquad g_s=u_s^4g,\\qquad K_s=u_s^2K.$$ These data are complete up to $B$ and satisfy DEC, strictly for $s>0$. If $\\theta_+\\le0$ on $B$, their boundary expansion remains nonpositive and is strictly negative for $s>0$. Their decay exponent can be taken to be $\\min(q,1)>1/2$, their constraint densities are integrable, and $$\\label{n3:reduction:strict-charges}\n E_s=E+sA_\\phi,\\qquad P_s=P,\n \\qquad A_\\phi=-\\frac{L_\\phi}{2\\pi}>0.$$ Their full enclosing infima satisfy $$\\label{n3:reduction:strict-areas}\n a_g(B)\\le a_{g_s}(B)\n       \\le (1+s\\|\\phi\\|_\\infty)^4a_g(B).$$ In particular $E_s\\to E$ and $a_{g_s}(B)\\to a_g(B)$ as $s\\downarrow0$. No sign assumption on the ADM vector is needed.*\n\n*If $K$ is compactly supported and the metric has symbol estimates of all orders with $g-\\delta=O(r^{-1})$, the function can instead be chosen with $\\phi=O_k(r^{-1})$ for every $k$, while retaining Equations <a href=\"#n3:reduction:strict-boundary\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:reduction:strict-boundary\">[n3:reduction:strict-boundary]</a> and <a href=\"#n3:reduction:strict-source\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"n3:reduction:strict-source\">[n3:reduction:strict-source]</a>.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.9"
        }
      ],

      "proof_anchor": "proof-stmt-n3-reduction-strict-direction"

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-enclosing-area-mass-bound**: The invariant ADM mass bounds the full enclosing-area infimum under the stated strong differentiated decay, dominant energy condition, integrability, finite-charge and weak future trapping hypotheses.
- **invariant-weak-decay-conclusions**: In dimensions three and four, the weaker differentiated decay suffices for positive enclosing area, future timelikeness and the enclosing-area mass inequality.
- **invariant-full-cut-accounting**: Enclosing area uses the entire intrinsic boundary of an admissible connected outer domain, including every component and any boundary-coincident portions; attainment of the infimum is unnecessary.
- **invariant-filled-flux-normalization**: For a global filled-system solution satisfying the specified floor, upper bound and end estimates, the divergence flux determines the ADM energy change and gives the stated upper energy estimate with a polynomial penalty error.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-horizon-area-substitution**: Replace the enclosing infimum by the boundary's own area. -> The substituted area can exceed the least area of an enclosing cut, so the resulting stronger bound is not supplied by the theorem.
- **anti-use-unverified-energy-and-trapping**: Apply the mass bound to data without establishing the dominant energy condition, integrability or the specified future expansion sign. -> The original-data hypotheses required for the mass comparison have not been established.
- **anti-use-interchanged-limits**: Take an elliptic limit in the large deformation parameter or use arbitrary parameter-dependent derivative estimates as polynomial estimates. -> The proof supplies exhaustion at each fixed parameter and a subsequent numerical limit; the required uniform derivative control for the proposed interchange is absent.
- **anti-use-finite-sampling-as-certificate**: Certify the full geometric inequality from sampled metrics, a finite truncation or agreement of discretized solvers. -> Finite samples do not establish the global smooth solution, end asymptotics, perimeter minimization or limiting comparisons required by the argument.
- **anti-use-equality-classification**: Infer a classification of the original spacetime data solely from equality in the numerical bound. -> Sharpness and an equality model do not supply the separate variational and horizon analysis required for rigidity of the original data.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The principal result concerns smooth complete noncompact initial-data exteriors and an infimum over full enclosing cuts. Its deformation requires global elliptic existence and perimeter minimization, followed by analytic limiting arguments; the paper supplies no finite algorithm with a terminating certificate for these hypotheses or conclusions. The source explicitly states: "The infimum need not be attained." It also states: "In particular, this proof takes no elliptic limit as $N\to\infty$ and imposes no equation on a limiting singular hypersurface." Finite algebra checks would cover only subsidiary identities and would not certify the geometric inequality.

A software validator would require additional approximation and certification results. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The geometric deformation is an existence result for smooth initial data and minimizing frontiers. It supplies no discrete evolution rule or simulation error bound. |
| tools | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The enclosing quantity ranges over entire intrinsic boundaries of admissible outer domains, and its infimum need not be attained. The paper does not construct a finite cut-search utility. |
| algorithms | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The coupled equations are solved through compactness, degree theory and exhaustion. These arguments establish existence without a terminating finite algorithm or a computational complexity guarantee. |

Singular frontiers and boundary coincidence would require representation choices beyond the stated construction. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The local estimates control derivatives of continuous solutions at fixed deformation parameter. They specify no arithmetic kernel, memory layout or parallel execution contract for an accelerator. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The compact constraint inverses concern smooth tensor sources orthogonal to affine functions and Euclidean Killing fields. They provide no cryptographic primitive, adversary model or security reduction. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The natural-growth estimate concerns a bounded classical solution with ellipticity and source-mass assumptions. It provides no learning construction or guarantee that a fitted surrogate satisfies those assumptions. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Perimeter minimization supplies an analytic obstacle enclosure through the direct method. The paper does not provide a finite optimisation formulation, an effective stopping criterion or a certified discretization. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The construction fixes the deformation parameter before exhausting the outer radii, then uses separate numerical limits. This order supplies no distributed protocol or guarantee for independently advancing coupled approximations. |
| other (Mathematical general relativity and geometric analysis) | True | strong | adaptable | inferred | The positive-shell construction gives a concrete continuous transformation of initial data: a nonnegative radial conformal factor, constant near the boundary, raises ADM energy while preserving momentum, the dominant energy condition and weak future trapping, and increases every full-cut area. This supports analytic comparison arguments; implementing it numerically requires additional certification. |

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove the sharp spacetime Penrose inequality for smooth one-ended initial-data exteriors in every spatial dimension <i>n</i> ≥ 3, under the dominant energy condition, weak future trapping, the stated differentiated decay and positive enclosing area. These hypotheses force the ADM energy-momentum to be future timelike. Area is the infimum over full enclosing cuts in the original metric. In dimensions three and four, two metric derivatives and one tensor derivative suffice, and both positive enclosing area and future timelikeness follow from the hypotheses.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### The inequality and its geometric quantity

The Penrose inequality asks how much mass is required to surround a trapped region. Its origin is a test of cosmic censorship: a collapsing configuration should settle to a black hole, radiation should carry energy away, and the horizon area should not decrease. Penrose’s null-shell argument made this comparison concrete (Penrose 1973) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Penrose1973](#ref-Penrose1973)]. An initial-data theorem must express it using only a Riemannian metric, a second fundamental form and a specified enclosing area.

The choice of area is part of the problem. A surface outside an apparent horizon can have smaller area than the horizon itself. Ben-Dov gave spherically symmetric examples satisfying the dominant energy condition for which the bound using the apparent horizon’s own area fails (Ben-Dov 2004) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[BenDov2004](#ref-BenDov2004)]. Carrasco and Mars found a different obstruction for generalized apparent horizons: their counterexamples already have an outer area-minimizing generalized horizon (Carrasco and Mars 2010) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[CarrascoMars2010](#ref-CarrascoMars2010)]. Thus a mass–area statement must specify both its trapping condition and its enclosing class. We use instead the infimum of the areas of all full cuts separating the boundary from infinity. Every component counts, including any part coincident with the boundary. The mass is the Lorentz-invariant length of the ADM energy-momentum vector. These choices lead to the following precise formulation.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### Data, area and statements

<a id="stmt-def-data"></a>
<div id="def:data" class="definition">

**Definition 1** (Initial-data exterior). Let $n\geq3$ and let $\Omega$ be a smooth connected orientable $n$-manifold with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$. The metric $g$ and symmetric covariant two-tensor $K$ are smooth up to $S$, and $g$ is complete with $S$ included. Outside a compact set, $\Omega$ is a single coordinate end $\{x\in\mathbb R^n:|x|>R_0\}$. Thus there are no additional ends hidden in the compact-complement condition.

<a id="eq:setting:constraints"></a>
Write $R_g$ for scalar curvature and $\nabla$ for the connection of $g$. Write $\tau=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK$. Our constraint normalization is $$\label{eq:setting:constraints}
 2\mu=R_g+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)^2-|K|_g^2,\qquad
 J_i=\nabla^j\bigl(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\bigr).$$ The dominant energy condition is $\mu\geq|J|_g$. We require $\mu,|J|_g\in L^1(\Omega,dV_g)$. Along $S$ the unit normal $\nu$ points into $\Omega$, toward the end. Its future expansion is $$\theta_+=H_S+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK,\qquad
 H_S=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_S\nu,\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK=(g^{ij}-\nu^i\nu^j)K_{ij}.$$ The boundary is weakly future trapped when $\theta_+\leq0$ on every component. No condition is imposed on the other null expansion.

<a id="eq:setting:energy"></a>
<a id="eq:setting:momentum"></a>
For coordinate tensors, $T=O_j(r^{-a})$ means $|\partial^\alpha T|\leq C_\alpha r^{-a-|\alpha|}$ for $|\alpha|\leq j$, where $r=|x|$. The decay orders will be specified in each theorem. Set $k=n-1$ and $\omega=\omega_{n-1}=|\mathbb S^{n-1}|$. The Laplacian is $\Delta=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}\nabla$ and symmetrization includes a factor $1/2$. We require the finite ADM limits $$\begin{aligned}
 E&=\frac{1}{2(n-1)\omega_{n-1}}\lim_{R\to\infty}
  \int_{|x|=R}(\partial_jg_{ij}-\partial_i g_{jj})
       n_\delta^i\,dA_\delta,\label{eq:setting:energy}\\
 P_i&=\frac{1}{(n-1)\omega_{n-1}}\lim_{R\to\infty}
  \int_{|x|=R}\bigl(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij}\bigr)
       n_\delta^j\,dA_\delta.\label{eq:setting:momentum}
\end{aligned}$$ Here $n_\delta$ and $dA_\delta$ are Euclidean. If $E>|P|_\delta$, define $m=(E^2-|P|_\delta^2)^{1/2}$.

</div>

<a id="stmt-def-fullcuts"></a>
<div id="def:fullcuts" class="definition">

**Definition 2** (Full enclosing cuts). A *full enclosing cut* is the entire intrinsic manifold boundary $\Gamma=\partial D$ of a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D\subset\Omega$. We require $D$ to be closed in $\Omega$, its manifold interior to lie in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, and $D$ to contain the whole sufficiently distant end. Its full boundary must be compact, smooth, embedded and two-sided. In particular, $D=\Omega$ is admissible and has boundary $S$. Define <a id="eq:setting:minarea"></a>$$\label{eq:setting:minarea}
 A_{\min,g}(S)=\inf_D\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(\partial D).$$ The use of intrinsic boundary ensures that coincident portions of $S$ are counted. A cut need not be connected, trapped or minimal. The infimum need not be attained.

</div>

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

<a id="eq:setting:main"></a>
**Theorem 3** (The enclosing-area Penrose inequality). *Let $(\Omega^n,g,K)$ be the smooth one-ended exterior specified above, with integrable constraint densities, finite ADM limits, dominant energy condition and weakly future trapped boundary. Suppose $$g-\delta=O_6(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_5(r^{-1-q}),\qquad
 \frac{n-2}{2}<q<n-2,$$ and assume $E>|P|_\delta$ and $A_{\min,g}(S)>0$. Then $$\label{eq:setting:main}
 m\geq\frac12\left(\frac{A_{\min,g}(S)}{\omega_{n-1}}
                 \right)^{\frac{n-2}{n-1}}.$$ The coefficient and exponent are sharp in each dimension $n\geq3$.*

</div>

Thus the enclosing-area form of the spacetime Penrose conjecture holds in this class. Neither outermostness nor outer area minimization of $S$ is assumed. The second fundamental form is arbitrary, and no spin, vacuum or interior-topology hypothesis is imposed. The time-symmetric Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior of mass $m>0$ has $A_{\min,g}(S)=\omega_{n-1}(2m)^{(n-1)/(n-2)}$ and attains equality.

<a id="stmt-cor-automatic-timelikeness"></a>
<div id="cor:automatic-timelikeness" class="corollary">

**Corollary 4** (Automatic future timelikeness in the strong-decay class). *Assume all hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">3</a> except the inequality $E>|P|_\delta$. In particular, retain the one-ended exterior, the $O_6/O_5$ decay with $(n-2)/2<q<n-2$, and $A_{\min,g}(S)>0$. Then $E>|P|_\delta$, and Equation <a href="#eq:setting:main" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:main">[eq:setting:main]</a> holds.*

</div>

The proof follows the numerical deduction in Section <a href="#sec:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:comparison">2</a>.

<a id="stmt-thm-low"></a>
<div id="thm:low" class="theorem">

**Theorem 5** (Weaker decay in dimensions three and four). *Let $n=3$ or $n=4$. Let $(\Omega^n,g,K)$ be the smooth one-ended exterior specified above, with integrable constraint densities, finite ADM limits, dominant energy condition and weakly future trapped boundary. Assume $$g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\qquad q>\frac{n-2}{2}.$$ Then $A_{\min,g}(S)>0$, $E>|P|_\delta$, and <a href="#eq:setting:main" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:main">[eq:setting:main]</a> holds.*

</div>

Here positive enclosing area and timelikeness are both conclusions, and no extra decay is required of $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK$. The two derivative regimes concern the original data. After preparation, both lead to ends with estimates at every fixed derivative order, allowing one common deformation theorem to prove the numerical bound.

There are also designated-end formulations for finitely many ends, with different area classes in dimensions three and four. In the three-dimensional complete-data formulation the chosen outer region may retain other ends; in four dimensions its connected outer domain excludes their distant tails. Sections <a href="#sec:weak3" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:weak3">7</a> and <a href="#sec:weak4" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:weak4">[sec:weak4]</a> give their precise definitions and proofs. Their reduction to the one-ended inequality compares the two enclosing infima in the needed direction; it does not identify them. The one-ended statements above isolate the common numerical construction. Equality for the original data requires additional horizon assumptions and a separate variational argument.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### From time symmetry to spacetime data

When $K=0$, the dominant energy condition becomes $R_g\geq0$ and a marginal boundary is minimal. Geroch introduced the connected-surface Hawking-mass monotonicity underlying smooth inverse mean curvature flow (Geroch 1973) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Geroch1973](#ref-Geroch1973)]. Jang and Wald related this method to the Penrose bound under the assumption that a classical flow runs from the inner boundary to asymptotically round spheres (Jang and Wald 1977) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[JangWald1977](#ref-JangWald1977)]; Huisken and Ilmanen recount these precursors in (Huisken and Ilmanen 2001, 359) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[HuiskenIlmanen2001](#ref-HuiskenIlmanen2001)]. Two different flow methods then established the three-dimensional Riemannian inequality. Huisken and Ilmanen’s weak inverse mean curvature flow allows jumps while preserving the Hawking mass comparison; its bound applies to each connected component of an outermost minimal boundary (Huisken and Ilmanen 2001) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[HuiskenIlmanen2001](#ref-HuiskenIlmanen2001)]. Bray’s conformal flow changes the metric, preserving the horizon area and making mass nonincreasing, and proves the sharp bound for the total area of a possibly disconnected horizon (Bray 2001) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[Bray2001](#ref-Bray2001)]. Bray and Lee extended that method through dimension seven (Bray and Lee 2009) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[BrayLee2009](#ref-BrayLee2009)]. Their numerical theorem requires no spin assumption; the additional spin hypothesis in the published statement belongs to its equality conclusion.

Above dimension seven, minimizing frontiers may be singular. Bi and Zhu extend conformal flow to this setting. Their revised theorem treats almost-minimizing Caccioppoli boundaries with minimal regular part, outermost minimizing enclosure and a metric extending with the stated regularity across the boundary (Bi and Zhu 2026, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[BiZhu2026v2](#ref-BiZhu2026v2)]. Their work supplies the ancestry of the separation, mass–capacity and convergence arguments used for the Riemannian endpoint here. The exact version we need allows all components of a locally minimizing and outer-minimizing frontier; its full proof is part of the Riemannian argument described below.

Nonzero $K$ introduces a different difficulty: neither scalar curvature nor the boundary mean curvature has the required Riemannian sign. Jang introduced a graph equation for extending Geroch’s positive-energy argument beyond time symmetry (Jang 1978) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[Jang1978](#ref-Jang1978)]. Schoen and Yau’s minimal-surface argument established the three-dimensional Riemannian positive-mass theorem (Schoen and Yau 1979) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[SchoenYau1979](#ref-SchoenYau1979)]. Their spacetime proof combined Jang’s equation with conformal deformation and a treatment of graph blow-up to prove positive energy for general three-dimensional initial data (Schoen and Yau 1981) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[SchoenYau1981](#ref-SchoenYau1981)]. The Penrose problem asks more of the deformation: a lower bound for enclosing area must survive along with the mass comparison. Malec and Ó Murchadha explained the obstruction to obtaining both controls from the direct classical-Jang and conformal-deformation scheme, even in spherical symmetry (Malec and Ó Murchadha 2004) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[Malec](#ref-Malec)].

In spherical symmetry, Malec and Ó Murchadha proved the inequality for maximal data, and Hayward obtained it from monotonicity of the Misner–Sharp energy in untrapped regions without that maximality restriction (Malec and Ó Murchadha 1994; Hayward 1996) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[MalecOMurchadha1994](#ref-MalecOMurchadha1994), [Hayward1996](#ref-Hayward1996)]. Bray and Khuri introduced a warped graph and a generalized Schoen–Yau scalar-curvature identity (Bray and Khuri 2010, 2011) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[BrayKhuri2010](#ref-BrayKhuri2010), [BrayKhuri2011](#ref-BrayKhuri2011)]. On solutions of the generalized Jang equation, the identity separates the nonnegative dominant-energy contribution and square terms from a divergence. It does not by itself solve the equations needed to control that divergence. They gave a new proof in spherical symmetry and proposed coupled systems for the general problem. Han and Khuri established existence and boundary blow-up for prescribed warping factors with suitable boundary and asymptotic behavior (Han and Khuri 2013) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[HanKhuri](#ref-HanKhuri)]. Jaracz later constructed spherical data for which one particular coupling, generalized Jang with zero divergence, has no smooth radial solution with the required positive warp and asymptotics (Jaracz 2023) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[Jaracz2023](#ref-Jaracz2023)]. That obstruction concerns the specified coupling and radial solution class.

Sharp spacetime results are also known beyond the spherical three-dimensional case. Bryden, Khuri and Sormani proved the sharp inequality and Schwarzschild rigidity in spherical symmetry in every spatial dimension (Bryden, Khuri, and Sormani 2021) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[BrydenKhuriSormani2021](#ref-BrydenKhuriSormani2021)]. Khuri and Kunduri proved a sharp spacetime inequality for $\mathrm{SU}(\ell+1)$-invariant data of dimension $2(\ell+1)$; their result for the full cohomogeneity-one class is Riemannian (Khuri and Kunduri 2025) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[KhuriKunduri2025](#ref-KhuriKunduri2025)].

For nonsymmetric three-dimensional asymptotically flat data, Allen, Bryden, Kazaras and Khuri proved a universal invariant-mass bound with a suboptimal constant under their asymptotic hypotheses, including extra decay of $\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK$ (Allen et al. 2025) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[AllenBrydenKazarasKhuri2025](#ref-AllenBrydenKazarasKhuri2025)]. For each end, their statement uses at least one outermost collection of future or past marginal components and its least enclosing area. Theorems <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">3</a> and <a href="#thm:low" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:low">5</a> give the sharp coefficient under the original-data hypotheses above, using full enclosing cuts for any weakly future trapped boundary.

Other nonsymmetric results concern different hypotheses and area quantities. Ellithy’s inequality bounds the total area of outermost future apparent-horizon sections under a quasi-final-state condition on the future development, negative ingoing expansion, and a piecewise smooth horizon tube with finitely many area-nondecreasing jumps (Ellithy 2026, Theorem 4.12) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[Ellithy2026](#ref-Ellithy2026)]. Dong’s pure-trace theorem gives the bound for each connected generalized-horizon component (Dong 2026b, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[Dong2026Sigma](#ref-Dong2026Sigma)]; his two-convex theorem assumes a connected outermost past apparent horizon (Dong 2026a, Theorem 1.2) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[Dong2026TwoConvex](#ref-Dong2026TwoConvex)]. In the latter class the stated asymptotic restrictions force zero ADM linear momentum, as noted in (Dong 2026a, Remark 1.3) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[Dong2026TwoConvex](#ref-Dong2026TwoConvex)]. These area and tensor assumptions are distinct from the full enclosing cuts and arbitrary second fundamental forms in our statements. Mars surveys the underlying alternatives in formulating the initial-data Penrose problem (Mars 2009) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[Mars2009](#ref-Mars2009)].

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### How the proof controls curvature, mass and area

The numerical argument first prepares the end, then performs one filled graph and conformal deformation. The preparation replaces the distant end by a vacuum reference slice with matching charges, bends that slice to rest, and repairs the constraints while comparing every full enclosing cut. Its output has compactly supported $K$, strict dominant energy condition and strict boundary trapping. In dimensions three and four the weak-decay preparation provides the same differentiated output. The three-dimensional enclosing infima converge to the original one; in four dimensions the available lower comparison is sufficient. The finite-stage data, rather than a formal limiting object, enter the common deformation theorem.

Fix a prepared exterior $(\Omega,g_0,K_0)$, with energy $E_0$ and enclosing area $A_0=A_{\min,g_0}(S)$. For each small $\varepsilon>0$, the deformation theorem constructs a family of smooth metrics indexed by a large parameter $N$. Each metric has a minimizing frontier lying in the original exterior and separating its inner boundary from infinity, with area at least $e^{-(n-1)\varepsilon}A_0$, nonnegative scalar curvature outside that frontier, and energy at most $E_0$ plus an error tending to zero as $N\to\infty$. The Riemannian numerical inequality therefore gives $$E_0\geq
 \frac12\left(\frac{e^{-(n-1)\varepsilon}A_0}
 {\omega_{n-1}}\right)^{\frac{n-2}{n-1}}$$ after $N\to\infty$. Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ proves the prepared inequality. Only then do we remove the end preparation. No metric at $N=\infty$ is needed.

The construction must explain all three estimates together. We fill the inner boundary smoothly and solve for a graph height and a conformal factor on the resulting manifold without boundary. The conformal factor has a lower bound, protecting the area of every enclosing cut. The curvature identity separates the dominant energy term, coercive squares and a divergence. In contrast to the zero-divergence coupling, the divergence has a specified nonzero source term; its integral controls the change of mass. Compared with the Schoen–Yau and Bray–Khuri identities (Schoen and Yau 1981; Bray and Khuri 2011) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[SchoenYau1981](#ref-SchoenYau1981), [BrayKhuri2011](#ref-BrayKhuri2011)], the trace equation and the divergence source are modified to enforce these simultaneous controls.

Global solvability is the analytic part of this construction. Height comparison and a barrier argument establish the lower conformal bound. Testing the scalar divergence equation and applying a Sobolev inequality on the graph, based on Michael–Simon (Michael and Simon 1973) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[MichaelSimon1973](#ref-MichaelSimon1973)], yield the complementary upper estimate before uniform ellipticity is available. Together these bounds control graph distortion and make the equations uniformly elliptic for each fixed $N$. Separate scalar regularity estimates treat the trace equation, whose distinguished direction is the solution’s gradient, and the divergence equation, which has quadratic gradient growth. They supply the control needed for continuation and exhaustion. These steps prove solvability of this particular coupled system; prescribed-warp existence for another system is not used as a substitute.

The filling removes inner boundary flux, but a minimizing enclosure might enter the filled region. We prevent this by a further conformal change, large deep inside the filling and small near infinity. Two-sided density estimates force the minimizing frontier away from the interior obstacle and into the band where scalar curvature has the correct sign. This is why scalar-curvature improvement alone would not finish the proof: the location and full area of the enclosure must be controlled.

For dimensions three through seven, Bray–Lee’s numerical theorem supplies the Riemannian endpoint. In higher dimensions the detached frontier can have a singular set of dimension at most $n-8$. The required endpoint is the minimizing-frontier theorem, including its conformal flow, separation, smoothing and limiting arguments. We use the complete companion argument of (OpenAI 2026b) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[RiemannianCompanion](#ref-RiemannianCompanion)]; Section <a href="#sec:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:comparison">2</a> quotes the precise mathematical input. Its numerical application uses the stated second-order asymptotic decay and weak-boundary hypotheses. Only the numerical bound is needed; no Riemannian equality theorem or all-orders expansion of the input metric at infinity is used. The endpoint thus requires control of both the singular frontier and the asymptotically flat end.

Section <a href="#sec:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:comparison">2</a> first states the prepared geometric output and proves the numerical comparison. Section <a href="#sec:end" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:end">3</a> prepares the strongly decaying original end. Sections <a href="#sec:scalar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:scalar">4</a> and <a href="#sec:elliptic" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:elliptic">[sec:elliptic]</a> derive the curvature identity and solve the filled system. Section <a href="#sec:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:height">6</a> locates the minimizing enclosure. Sections <a href="#sec:weak3" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:weak3">7</a> and <a href="#sec:weak4" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:weak4">[sec:weak4]</a> give the complete weak-decay preparations and their distinct designated-end transfers. The companion *Boundary graph deformations for the spacetime Penrose inequality* (OpenAI 2026a) <a id="pm-cite-30"></a>[[BoundaryCompanion](#ref-BoundaryCompanion)] <a id="pm-cite-31"></a>[[RigidityCompanion](#ref-RigidityCompanion)] studies what changes when one keeps an actual inner boundary, including its signed flux, or retains a decaying tensor in a maximal-data construction. It provides alternative analytic tools. The companion *Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality* (OpenAI 2026c) returns to the original $g$ and $K$ through variation, a causal adjoint system and static classification. These alternative methods and equality results are not premises of the numerical argument proved here.

<a id="sec:comparison"></a>
### The prepared geometric comparison

The central construction produces a Riemannian exterior whose energy is almost no larger than the energy of the input, while its full boundary area is almost no smaller than the input’s least enclosing area. This section states that construction in geometric terms and gives the complete numerical deduction. The following sections prove the construction. The data entering it are specified directly; they need not have been obtained by any particular preparation procedure.

<a id="stmt-def-prepared"></a>
<div id="def:prepared" class="definition">

<a id="eq:end:prepared"></a>
**Definition 6** (Prepared exterior). Let $(\Omega^n,g_0,K_0)$ be a smooth connected orientable one-ended exterior with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$, complete with $S$ included and with compact complement of its Euclidean coordinate end. Use the constraint and ADM conventions of Equations <a href="#eq:setting:constraints" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:constraints">[eq:setting:constraints]</a>–<a href="#eq:setting:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:momentum">[eq:setting:momentum]</a>. Let $\varrho$ be a smooth positive function on the closed exterior, equal to the coordinate radius on a distant tail. Require that, for some $0<\beta<1$ and $c>0$, $$\label{eq:end:prepared}
\begin{gathered}
 \operatorname{supp}K_0\text{ is compact},\qquad
 g_0-\delta=O_d(r^{2-n})\text{ for every fixed }d,\\
 R_{g_0}=O(r^{-n-\beta}),\qquad
 \mu_0-|J_0|_{g_0}\ge c\varrho^{-n-\beta},\qquad
 H_S+\operatorname{tr}_S K_0<0\text{ on every component of }S.
\end{gathered}$$ The constraint densities are integrable. The ADM momentum is $P_0=0$; write $E_0$ for the energy. Finally the full-cut infimum, with every component and all contact counted as in Definition <a href="#def:fullcuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:fullcuts">2</a>, is $A_0=A_{\min,g_0}(S)>0$.

</div>

Once one prepared datum has been fixed, we suppress its subscript and write $g,K,E,a$ for $g_0,K_0,E_0,A_0$. All constants in its deformation may depend on this fixed datum. A proper map comparing different prepared data is an output of end preparation, not an assumption in this definition.

The output below may have a singular frontier. For an enclosing-set exterior, length distance is computed by rectifiable paths in the closed exterior and may equal $+\infty$. Completeness means completeness on each finite-distance equivalence class; every frontier point and the full perimeter remain included.

<a id="stmt-prop-height-enclosure"></a>
<div id="prop:height:enclosure" class="theorem">

**Theorem 7** (The geometric deformation). *<span id="thm:prepared:deformation" label="thm:prepared:deformation"></span> Fix a prepared exterior and $0<\epsilon<1$. For all sufficiently large integers $N$ there is a connected enclosing-set exterior $X_N$, complete with its compact frontier $\Sigma_N$ included, in a smooth Riemannian ambient metric $\widetilde g_N$. It has one Euclidean coordinate end with compact complement, and <a id="eq:height:enclosure-estimates"></a>$$\label{eq:height:enclosure-estimates}
\begin{split}
 &R_{\widetilde g_N}\ge0,\quad R_{\widetilde g_N}\in L^1(X_N),
 \quad \widetilde g_N-\delta=O_2(r^{2-n}),\\
 &R_{\widetilde g_N}=O(r^{-n-\beta'})\quad\text{for some }\beta'>0,\\
 &E(\widetilde g_N)\le E_0+P_N(e^{-N\epsilon}+e^{-N\epsilon/2}),\\
 &\mathcal H^{n-1}_{\widetilde g_N}(\Sigma_N)
       \ge e^{-(n-1)\epsilon}A_0.
\end{split}$$ Here $P_N$ is a polynomial in $N$, with coefficients depending on the fixed datum and $\epsilon$. The metric is smooth through the frontier. The whole frontier is outer minimizing and locally perimeter minimizing as the boundary of its filled side. It is smooth embedded minimal away from a compact singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-8$; for $3\le n\le7$ the singular set is empty. Its area counts every component.*

</div>

The proof is completed in Section <a href="#sec:height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:height">6</a>. The analytic construction in Sections <a href="#sec:scalar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:scalar">4</a> and <a href="#sec:elliptic" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:elliptic">[sec:elliptic]</a> takes place on a smooth filling and yields the energy estimate before any frontier is selected. The height argument then gives a detached minimizing frontier and the lower bound for its full area.

Here is the precise Riemannian input from the complete companion *Conformal flow and the Riemannian Penrose inequality with minimizing frontiers* (OpenAI 2026b) <a id="pm-cite-32"></a>[[RiemannianCompanion](#ref-RiemannianCompanion)]. We use its Theorem 1.1 in the following form.

> Let $X^n$ be a connected complete enclosing-set exterior, including its compact frontier $\Sigma$, with a metric $\gamma$ smooth through that frontier. Suppose there is one Euclidean coordinate end with compact complement, $\gamma-\delta=O_2(r^{-\tau})$ with $\tau>(n-2)/2$, and $R_\gamma\ge0$, $R_\gamma\in L^1$, and $R_\gamma=O(r^{-n-\beta})$ for some $\beta>0$. Suppose its full frontier is outer minimizing and locally perimeter minimizing as the boundary of the filled side, allowing compactly supported variations on either side. Its regular part is a smooth embedded minimal hypersurface. Its singular set has Hausdorff dimension at most $n-8$. Then $$E(\gamma)\ge\frac12
>  \left(\frac{\mathcal H^{n-1}_\gamma(\Sigma)}{\omega_{n-1}}
>  \right)^{(n-2)/(n-1)}.$$ The assertion includes zero frontier area and imposes neither a spin condition nor connectedness of the frontier.

The smooth numerical theorem of Bray–Lee (Bray and Lee 2009, Theorem 1.4) <a id="pm-cite-33"></a>[[BrayLee2009](#ref-BrayLee2009)] is an alternative in dimensions three through seven. In higher dimensions the companion retains the full singular-frontier argument. Its conformal-flow ancestry includes Bi–Zhu’s version 2 area-before-nesting and singular separation arguments (Bi and Zhu 2026) <a id="pm-cite-34"></a>[[BiZhu2026v2](#ref-BiZhu2026v2)]. The independent smooth positive-mass input is Brendle–Wang (Brendle and Wang 2026, Corollary 1.6) <a id="pm-cite-35"></a>[[BrendleWang2026](#ref-BrendleWang2026)], applied there to constructed smooth complete boundaryless approximants with strictly positive scalar curvature and the required differentiated end. Those stronger approximant hypotheses are not additional assumptions on $X$.

<a id="stmt-thm-numerical-prepared"></a>
<div id="thm:numerical:prepared" class="theorem">

**Theorem 8** (The prepared energy inequality). *Every exterior in Definition <a href="#def:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:prepared">6</a> satisfies <a id="eq:height:prepared-inequality"></a>$$\label{eq:height:prepared-inequality}
 E_0\ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_0}{\omega}\right)^{(n-2)/(n-1)}.$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-numerical-prepared"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-numerical-prepared</summary>

*Proof.* Fix the datum and $\epsilon$. Apply the quoted Riemannian theorem to the actual exterior $X_N$ furnished by Theorem <a href="#thm:prepared:deformation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:prepared:deformation">[thm:prepared:deformation]</a>. Its metric is smooth through the compact frontier; its closure is complete and its open exterior is connected. The end has compact complement and decay exponent $n-2>(n-2)/2$. Its scalar curvature is nonnegative and integrable with the required pointwise decay. The whole frontier is outer minimizing and locally perimeter minimizing, hence has minimal regular part and singular dimension at most $n-8$. These verify each receiving hypothesis. We obtain $$E_0+P_N(e^{-N\epsilon}+e^{-N\epsilon/2})
 \ge E(\widetilde g_N)
 \ge\frac12\left(
 \frac{\mathcal H^{n-1}_{\widetilde g_N}(\Sigma_N)}\omega
 \right)^{(n-2)/(n-1)}
 \ge\frac12\left(\frac{e^{-(n-1)\epsilon}A_0}\omega
 \right)^{(n-2)/(n-1)}.$$ First let $N\to\infty$; exponential decay beats the fixed polynomial. Then let $\epsilon\downarrow0$. These are limits of numbers. The exhaustion constructing a smooth solution at each fixed $N$ is completed before this argument, and no metric at $N=\infty$ is required. Since $A_0>0$, this also proves $E_0>0$. ◻

</details>

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-numerical-prepared-2"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-numerical-prepared</summary>

*Deduction of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">3</a>.* Proposition <a href="#prop:end:reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:end:reduction">9</a>, proved in the next section, supplies prepared data with energies $E_j\to
m=\sqrt{E^2-|P|^2}$ and enclosing infima $A_j\ge(1-o(1))A_{\min,g}(S)$. Apply Theorem <a href="#thm:numerical:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:numerical:prepared">8</a> to each prepared datum, completing all its fixed-data limits first. Then $$m\ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_{\min,g}(S)}\omega\right)^{(n-2)/(n-1)}.$$ No estimate uniform in the preparation index is used.

For sharpness, let $M>0$, $r_M=(2M)^{1/(n-2)}$, and take the static Schwarzschild–Tangherlini slice $$g=\frac{dr^2}{1-2M/r^{n-2}}+r^2\sigma_{n-1},\quad K=0,
 \qquad r\ge r_M.$$ Proper distance from the horizon makes this a smooth complete metric with minimal compact boundary. Its scalar curvature is zero, and its ADM vector is $(M,0)$. Radial projection to the sphere of radius $r_M$ has $(n-1)$-Jacobian at most one. More explicitly the pullback of that sphere’s area form is closed with comass at most one; Stokes’ theorem on an end truncation of any full outer domain shows that its integral over the entire cut is $\omega r_M^{n-1}$. Thus every full cut has area at least that number, while the boundary itself attains it. Consequently $A_{\min}=\omega(2M)^{(n-1)/(n-2)}$ and equality holds. ◻

</details>

The same numerical bound forces future timelikeness once a positive enclosing area is retained under an energy-raising conformal change.

<details id="proof-stmt-thm-numerical-prepared-3"><summary>Proof of stmt-thm-numerical-prepared</summary>

*Proof of Corollary <a href="#cor:automatic-timelikeness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cor:automatic-timelikeness">4</a>.* If instead $E\le |P|_\delta$, choose $\varepsilon_j>0$ tending to zero and put $$\lambda_j=\frac{|P|_\delta+\varepsilon_j-E}{2}>0.$$ Lemma <a href="#lem:end:positive-shell" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:end:positive-shell">14</a>, proved in the final subsection of Section <a href="#sec:end" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:end">3</a>, gives, separately for each $j$, data satisfying the same one-ended strong-decay, constraint and trapping hypotheses, with $$E_j=|P|_\delta+\varepsilon_j,\qquad P_j=P,\qquad
 A_{\min,g_j}(S)\ge A_{\min,g}(S)>0.$$ Their ADM vectors are future timelike, so Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">3</a> gives $$\sqrt{(|P|_\delta+\varepsilon_j)^2-|P|_\delta^2}
 \ge \frac12\left(\frac{A_{\min,g}(S)}{\omega_{n-1}}\right)^{
                   \frac{n-2}{n-1}}>0.$$ The right side is fixed and the left side tends to zero, a contradiction. The theorem is applied afresh to each datum; no estimate for its end preparation is required to be uniform near the null cone. Thus $E>|P|_\delta$, and Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">3</a> applies to the original data. ◻

</details>

The proofs for weak original decay appear in Sections <a href="#sec:weak3" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:weak3">7</a> and <a href="#sec:weak4" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:weak4">[sec:weak4]</a>. Their reductions reach Definition <a href="#def:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:prepared">6</a> by different means: three-dimensional enclosing areas converge fully, whereas the four-dimensional rest replacement gives the one-sided comparison needed by the numerical argument. The latter is followed by strictification at fixed replacement radius, with that strictification removed before the radius tends to infinity.

<a id="sec:end"></a>
### Preparing an end with zero momentum

Put $k=n-1$ and $p=n-2=k-1$. A radius function $\varrho$ below is smooth and positive on the closed exterior and equals the Euclidean radius on a sufficiently distant part of its coordinate end. Constants in the end-preparation argument may depend on the original data and on its fixed future-timelike ADM vector. In particular, no uniform estimate as $E-|P|\downarrow0$ is asserted. The final subsection supplies the positive-shell construction used in Section <a href="#sec:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:comparison">2</a> to prove automatic timelikeness; that construction does not assume timelikeness.

The target class is Definition <a href="#def:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:prepared">6</a>. The present task is to reach it while comparing every full cut with an original cut.

<a id="stmt-prop-end-reduction"></a>
<div id="prop:end:reduction" class="proposition">

<a id="eq:end:reduction-limits"></a>
**Proposition 9** (Reduction to a prepared exterior). *Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ be a smooth one-ended exterior as in Definition <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a>, with compact complement of its coordinate end and with $$g-\delta=O_6(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_5(r^{-1-q}),\qquad
 \frac{n-2}{2}<q<n-2.$$ Assume integrable constraint densities satisfying $\mu\ge|J|_g$, finite ADM limits satisfying $E>|P|$, and $\theta_+(S)\le0$ on every boundary component. Suppose that the full-cut infimum of Definition <a href="#def:fullcuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:fullcuts">2</a> is $a=A_{\min}^{g}(S)>0$, and put $m=(E^2-|P|^2)^{1/2}$. There are prepared data $(g_j,K_j)$ on the same exterior, with one fixed $\beta\in(0,1)$, numbers $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$, and proper diffeomorphisms $\Phi_j:\Omega\longrightarrow\Omega$ equal to the identity near $S$, such that $$\label{eq:end:reduction-limits}
 P_j=0,\qquad E_j\longrightarrow m,\qquad
 \Phi_j^*g\le(1+\epsilon_j)g_j,\qquad
 A_{\min}^{g_j}(S)\ge(1+\epsilon_j)^{-k/2}a.$$ The positive constant $c_j$ in Equation <a href="#eq:end:prepared" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:end:prepared">[eq:end:prepared]</a> and the end coordinates may depend on $j$.*

</div>

We first match the original energy and momentum with a boosted vacuum end. A compact annular correction joins the two ends with a constraint error whose total scale tends to zero. Within the vacuum region we then bend the slice to a static one, giving zero momentum. A positive conformal factor repairs the small annular error without decreasing the metric. A proper radial comparison map protects every full enclosing cut during the change of slice. For each already fixed replacement, a second scalar perturbation makes the energy condition and future trapping strict while changing the energy by a quantity tending to zero. The argument fixes the original boost throughout; it needs no estimates uniform as the ADM vector approaches the null cone.

An asymptotic change to a rest frame is also used by Allen, Bryden, Kazaras and Khuri in the invariant-mass step of (Allen et al. 2025, sec. 5) <a id="pm-cite-36"></a>[[AllenBrydenKazarasKhuri2025](#ref-AllenBrydenKazarasKhuri2025)]. Here the end is first replaced by an explicit vacuum model, and the proper comparison map in Proposition <a href="#prop:end:reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:end:reduction">9</a> controls every full cut during the replacement and bending.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
#### Conformal changes and a vacuum model with matching charges

The conformal identities below explain how a scalar function can improve the constraint inequality and the boundary expansion at the same time. We then compute the vacuum model’s charges directly in the ADM normalization used here.

<a id="eq:end:conformal"></a>
<a id="eq:end:conformal-U"></a>
For a smooth function $s$ set $g_s=e^{2s}g$ and $K_s=e^sK$. If $|v|_g\le1$, the corresponding vector in the new unit ball is $v_s=e^{-s}v$. The conformal connection formula and scalar curvature formula give $$\label{eq:end:conformal}
\begin{aligned}
 e^{2s}\bigl(\mu_s+J_s(v_s)\bigr)
 &=\mu+J(v)-k\Delta_gs-\frac{kp}{2}|ds|_g^2
                  +kK(\nabla s,v),\\
 e^s\theta_{+,s}&=\theta_++k\partial_\nu s.
\end{aligned}$$ Here the normal $\nu$ points into the exterior. For completeness, $\tau_s=e^{-s}\tau$, $|K_s|_{g_s}^2=e^{-2s}|K|_g^2$, and $$R_{g_s}=e^{-2s}\bigl(R_g-2k\Delta_gs-kp|ds|_g^2\bigr).$$ Writing $\pi=K-\tau g$, contraction of $\Gamma(g_s)^l_{ij}-\Gamma(g)^l_{ij}
=s_i\delta_j^l+s_j\delta_i^l-g_{ij}s^l$ yields $J_{s,i}=e^{-s}(J_i+kK_{ij}\nabla^js)$. The tangential trace of $K$ scales by $e^{-s}$ and $H_s=e^{-s}(H+k\partial_\nu s)$, proving both identities. In particular, if $s=2p^{-1}\log U$, $U>0$, the entire added term in the first identity is $$\label{eq:end:conformal-U}
 \frac{2k}{pU}\bigl(-\Delta_gU+K(\nabla U,v)\bigr).$$

<a id="stmt-lem-end-boost"></a>
<div id="lem:end:boost" class="lemma">

**Lemma 10** (Charges of a boosted Schwarzschild–Tangherlini end). *In the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime of geometric mass $M>0$, let $b,y$ be static time and isotropic spatial coordinates. Make the Lorentz change <a id="eq:end:boost-coordinates"></a>$$\label{eq:end:boost-coordinates}
 b=\gamma(T+vx^1),\qquad y^1=\gamma(x^1+vT),\qquad
 y^a=x^a\ (2\le a\le n),\qquad \gamma=(1-v^2)^{-1/2},$$ where $0\le v<1$. The induced data on $T=0$, oriented by the future normal, have <a id="eq:end:boost-charges"></a>$$\label{eq:end:boost-charges}
 E=\gamma M,\qquad P_1=\gamma Mv,\qquad P_a=0\ (a>1).$$ The metric and second fundamental form have the homogeneous leading terms computed below, with remainders $O_d(r^{-2p})$ and $O_d(r^{-2p-1})$, respectively, for every fixed derivative order $d$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-end-boost"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-end-boost</summary>

<a id="eq:end:boost-energy-vector"></a>
*Proof.* The exact isotropic metric is $$-\left(\frac{1-M/(2|y|^p)}{1+M/(2|y|^p)}\right)^2db^2
 +\left(1+\frac{M}{2|y|^p}\right)^{4/p}|dy|^2.$$ Its leading perturbation of Minkowski space is $2M|y|^{-p}(db^2+p^{-1}|dy|^2)$. On $T=0$ put $$\rho^2=\gamma^2(x^1)^2+\sum_{a=2}^n(x^a)^2,\qquad f=\rho^{-p},
 \qquad A=\gamma^2(v^2+p^{-1}),\quad B=p^{-1},\quad
 C=kp^{-1}\gamma^2v.$$ The nonzero relevant leading components of the spacetime perturbation $\mathsf H$ are $\mathsf H_{11}=2MAf$, $\mathsf H_{aa}=2MBf$, and $\mathsf H_{01}=2MCf$. Moreover $$\partial_1f=-p\gamma^2x^1\rho^{-n},\qquad
 \partial_af=-px^a\rho^{-n},\qquad
 \partial_Tf=-p\gamma^2vx^1\rho^{-n}.$$ Thus the energy flux vector $Q_i=\partial_j\mathsf H_{ij}
-\partial_i\mathsf H_{jj}$ satisfies $$Q_1=-2MkB\partial_1f=2Mk\gamma^2x^1\rho^{-n},\qquad
 Q_a=-2M(A+pB)\partial_af=2Mp(A+1)x^a\rho^{-n}.$$ Since $p(A+1)=k\gamma^2$, these expressions give the pointwise identity $$\label{eq:end:boost-energy-vector}
 Q_i=2Mk\gamma^2x_i\rho^{-n}.$$

<a id="eq:end:boost-momentum-tensor"></a>
The chosen sign of the second fundamental form gives, to first order, $$K_{ij}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_T\mathsf H_{ij}
                 -\partial_i\mathsf H_{0j}
                 -\partial_j\mathsf H_{0i}\bigr).$$ Direct substitution gives $$\begin{aligned}
 K_{11}&=M\gamma^4v(2p+1-pv^2)x^1\rho^{-n},&
 K_{aa}&=-M\gamma^2vx^1\rho^{-n},\\
 K_{1a}&=Mk\gamma^2vx^a\rho^{-n},&
 K_{ab}&=0\quad(a\ne b).
\end{aligned}$$ Their Euclidean trace is $M\gamma^4v(p+v^2)x^1\rho^{-n}$. Consequently, for the leading Euclidean trace reversal $\pi_{ij}=K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\delta K)\delta_{ij}$, $$\label{eq:end:boost-momentum-tensor}
 \pi_{1j}=Mk\gamma^2v x_j\rho^{-n},\qquad
 \pi_{a1}=Mk\gamma^2vx^a\rho^{-n},\qquad
 \pi_{ab}=-Mk\gamma^4vx^1\rho^{-n}\delta_{ab}.$$ Using the exact normal and the exact metric in the trace reversal changes these formulas by $O_d(r^{-2p-1})$. The energy remainder has first derivatives of this same order. Their sphere integrals are $O(r^{-p})$, and therefore vanish for every $n\ge3$.

<a id="eq:end:ellipsoid-integral"></a>
The ellipsoid $\{|\operatorname{diag}(\gamma,1,\ldots,1)x|<1\}$ has volume $\omega/(n\gamma)$. Polar integration therefore gives $$\label{eq:end:ellipsoid-integral}
 \int_{S^{n-1}}|\operatorname{diag}(\gamma,1,\ldots,1)\theta|^{-n}
 \,d\theta=\frac{\omega}{\gamma}.$$ Equations <a href="#eq:end:boost-energy-vector" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:end:boost-energy-vector">[eq:end:boost-energy-vector]</a> and <a href="#eq:end:boost-momentum-tensor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:end:boost-momentum-tensor">[eq:end:boost-momentum-tensor]</a>, divided by $2k\omega$ and $k\omega$, give $E=M\gamma$ and $P_1=M\gamma v$. The integrand of a transverse momentum row is a constant times $x^1x^a\rho^{-n}/r$, whose integral vanishes by reflection. ◻

</details>

For the original charges we now fix $M=m$, $v=|P|/E$, and rotate the first axis to the direction of $P$ when $P\ne0$. Lemma <a href="#lem:end:boost" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:end:boost">10</a> gives a model end $(g^{\mathrm b},K^{\mathrm b})$ with exactly the same charges. The parameter $v$ is fixed in all limits that follow.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
#### Joining the original and model ends

A direct cutoff need not preserve the dominant energy condition. Our immediate task is to remove its leading constraint error by compactly supported corrections. The obstructions to a compact correction are finitely many moments. Charge matching removes their constant limits, and integrability makes the remaining first moments small enough after rescaling.

Localized constraint deformation and the finite-dimensional obstruction from the adjoint kernel are central to the gluing methods of Corvino–Schoen (Corvino and Schoen 2006) <a id="pm-cite-37"></a>[[CorvinoSchoen2006](#ref-CorvinoSchoen2006)] and Chruściel–Delay (Chruściel and Delay 2003) <a id="pm-cite-38"></a>[[ChruscielDelay2003](#ref-ChruscielDelay2003)]. We use this methodological starting point, not an imported rest-end replacement theorem: the present data need not be vacuum, no parity is imposed, and both the energy inequality and every full enclosing cut must survive the replacement.

We give the compact correction explicitly because neither parity conditions nor convergence of center of mass or angular momentum is assumed. On Euclidean tensors define $$\mathsf S(h)=\partial_i\partial_j(h_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\delta h)\delta_{ij}),
 \qquad
 \mathsf D(b)_i=\partial_j(b_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\delta b)\delta_{ij}).$$ Their formal adjoint kernels relevant to compact support are, respectively, affine scalar functions and Euclidean Killing fields.

<a id="stmt-lem-end-compact-inverses"></a>
<div id="lem:end:compact-inverses" class="lemma">

**Lemma 11** (Compact right inverses). *Let $\mathcal A\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected Euclidean annulus and fix a compact subset of its interior. Smooth scalar sources supported in that subset with zero constant and first moments have smooth symmetric solutions of $\mathsf S(h)=f$ supported in a larger fixed compact subset of $\mathcal A$. Smooth vector sources with zero integrals against every Euclidean Killing field have similarly supported symmetric solutions of $\mathsf D(b)=F$. For $1<a<\infty$ and integers $d\ge0$, these solutions may be chosen linearly with estimates $$\|h\|_{W^{d+2,a}}\le C_{d,a}\|f\|_{W^{d,a}},\qquad
 \|b\|_{W^{d+1,a}}\le C_{d,a}\|F\|_{W^{d,a}}.$$ For arbitrary sources the same conclusions hold after subtracting fixed smooth moment bumps, whose coefficients are bounded by the absolute values of the respective moments.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-end-compact-inverses"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-end-compact-inverses</summary>

*Proof.* We use the compact scalar divergence inverse on a connected open set: a mean-zero smooth function supported in a fixed compact set has a compactly supported vector primitive, with one Sobolev derivative gained; the support and Sobolev mapping statements are given, for example, by the regularized Bogovskii operator in (Costabel and McIntosh 2010, sec. 3.1, Equation (3.13), Theorem 3.2, Corollaries 3.3–3.4, Remark 3.5, and Proposition 4.1(ii)) <a id="pm-cite-39"></a>[[CostabelMcIntosh2010](#ref-CostabelMcIntosh2010)]. Here is its local construction and the support issue. On a ball, choose a smooth unit-integral function supported in a smaller concentric ball and use the Bogovskii integral $$(\mathcal Bf)(x)=\int f(y)(x-y)
          \int_1^\infty\eta(y+t(x-y))t^{n-1}\,dt\,dy.$$ Differentiation in distributions gives $\mathop{\mathrm{div}}\mathcal Bf=f-\eta\int f=f$; the segments occurring in the integral remain in the ball. For compact input support and compact $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\eta$, their union is compact in that ball. The kernel is of order $1-n$, and its differentiated kernel has the cancellation of a Calderon–Zygmund kernel. The resulting $W^{d,a}$ estimate is the usual boundedness of that singular integral and its commutators with derivatives. Cover the prescribed support by finitely many balls compact in $\mathcal A$, connect them by a finite chain of overlapping such balls, and use a partition of unity. Transfer the means along the chain using unit-integral bumps in the overlaps. Each resulting ball source has mean zero; the sum of its ball primitives proves the stated inverse on $\mathcal A$, with fixed support and constants.

Apply it first to a scalar $f$ with its affine moments zero, obtaining $\partial_iv_i=f$. Compact support gives $\int v_i=-\int z_i f=0$. Apply the same inverse to each $v_i$ to obtain $\partial_jT_{ij}=v_i$. Then $Q=(T+T^{\mathsf t})/2$ has $\partial_i\partial_jQ_{ij}=f$. The tensor $h=Q-k^{-1}(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\delta Q)\delta$ has trace reversal $Q$, so $\mathsf S(h)=f$ with the asserted two-derivative gain.

For a vector source $F$, first solve $\partial_jB_{ij}=F_i$ row by row. Translation moments permit this solve. Rotation moments give $$0=\int(z_iF_j-z_jF_i)=\int(B_{ij}-B_{ji}).$$ Put $A_{ij}=(B_{ij}-B_{ji})/2$ and solve $\partial_lD_{ijl}=-A_{ij}$, choosing $D_{ijl}=-D_{jil}$. Set $$E_{ij}=\partial_l(D_{ijl}-D_{ilj}-D_{jli}),\qquad C_{ij}=B_{ij}+E_{ij}.$$ Index interchange gives $E_{ij}-E_{ji}=-2A_{ij}$ and $\partial_jE_{ij}=0$: the first two double derivatives cancel after interchanging $j,l$, and the last vanishes by skew symmetry in those indices. Thus $C$ is symmetric and $\partial_jC_{ij}=F_i$. Taking $b=C-k^{-1}(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\delta C)\delta$ proves the assertion, including the derivative count.

Finally take a nonnegative smooth bump supported in an open ball of $\mathcal A$. The Gram matrix of the affine functions, or of the vector Killing fields, with this weight is positive definite: a polynomial in either finite-dimensional space vanishing on that ball vanishes identically. Multiplying the basis elements by the bump and the inverse Gram matrix produces fixed dual moment bumps. Subtraction removes all moments with the stated bound on coefficients. ◻

</details>
