 E_{g_s}\longrightarrow E_g,
 \qquad A_*(g_s)\longrightarrow A_*(g)
 \quad\hbox{as }s\downarrow0.$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n4-lem-strictification"><summary>Proof of stmt-n4-lem-strictification</summary>

<a id="n4:eq:strictification-phi-decay"></a>
*Proof.* The generic strictification lemma, Lemma <a href="#lem:end:strict" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:end:strict">13</a>, applies to this fixed rest exterior. Indeed the exact static tail has $g-\delta=O_d(r^{-2})$ for every $d$, and $K$ is compactly supported. Choose any $1<q_*<2$ to express its $O_6/O_5$ bounds, set $n=4$, $k=3$, and take $\beta=\delta_1$. The condition $0<\delta_1<\min(1,q_*)$ is exactly the one required by that lemma. Its smooth nonnegative majorant can be chosen compactly supported: write it as $b_0\ge|K|_g$. The complete mixed-boundary continuation, uniform core and tail estimates, exhaustion, and differentiated-decay proof of that lemma therefore give a positive smooth solution of <a id="n4:eq:strictification-pde"></a>$$\label{n4:eq:strictification-pde}
 -\Delta_g\phi=b_0\sqrt{|\mathrm d\phi|_g^2+r^{-6}}+r^{-4-\delta_1},
 \qquad \partial_\nu\phi=-1,\qquad \phi\longrightarrow0.$$ The exponent $-6$ is $-2k$. The all-order clause of the same lemma gives $$\label{n4:eq:strictification-phi-decay}
 |\partial^j\phi|\le C_jr^{-2-j}\qquad(j\ge0).$$ This application occurs after rest replacement, so it uses no higher derivatives of the original weakly asymptotically flat end.

We now verify the geometric conclusions. Put $$F=b_0\sqrt{|\mathrm d\phi|^2+r^{-6}}+r^{-4-\delta_1}.$$ The inner outward normal is $-\nu$, and the finite-flux conclusion of the lemma is <a id="n4:eq:strictification-flux"></a>$$\label{n4:eq:strictification-flux}
 L_\phi=\lim_{T\to\infty}\int_{S_T}\partial_r\phi\,\mathrm dA_\delta
       =-|\partial M|_g-\int_MF\,\mathrm dV_g<0.$$ The geometric and Euclidean fluxes differ by $O(T^{-2})$ on the static tail, by <a href="#n4:eq:strictification-phi-decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:eq:strictification-phi-decay">[n4:eq:strictification-phi-decay]</a>.

Apply Lemma <a href="#n4:lem:conformal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:lem:conformal">51</a> with $u=e^{s\phi}$. It gives $$e^{2s\phi}(\mu_s-|J_s|_{g_s})
 \ge3s\bigl(r^{-4-\delta_1}-s|\mathrm d\phi|^2\bigr).$$ The number $B=\sup_M r^{4+\delta_1}|\mathrm d\phi|^2$ is finite: smoothness controls the compact core and the tail is $O(r^{-2+\delta_1})$. Choose $sB\le1/2$. This proves the global margin with $c_s=(3s/2)e^{-2s\|\phi\|_\infty}>0$. On each boundary component, $$\Theta_{K_s}=e^{-s\phi}(\Theta_K+3s\partial_\nu\phi)
            =e^{-s\phi}(\Theta_K-3s)<0.$$ Furthermore <a id="n4:eq:strictification-metric-comparison"></a>$$\label{n4:eq:strictification-metric-comparison}
 g\le g_s\le e^{2s\|\phi\|_\infty}g.$$ Thus completeness with the boundary included is preserved, and the tensor remains compactly supported. On the tail, $R_g=0$, $K_s=0$ and $$R_{g_s}=6e^{-2s\phi}
       \bigl(sr^{-4-\delta_1}-s^2|\mathrm d\phi|^2\bigr)
       =O(r^{-4-\delta_1}).$$ This proves the scalar decay and integrability there; the rest is smooth and compact. All differentiated metric bounds follow from <a href="#n4:eq:strictification-phi-decay" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:eq:strictification-phi-decay">[n4:eq:strictification-phi-decay]</a>, and momentum is zero because the tensor vanishes on a distant tail.

The leading metric change is $2s\phi\delta+O_1(r^{-4})$, whose energy flux numerator is $-6s\partial_i\phi+O(r^{-5})$. The latter remainder has vanishing sphere flux. Division by $6\omega_3$ therefore gives <a id="n4:eq:strictification-energy"></a>$$\label{n4:eq:strictification-energy}
 E_{g_s}-E_g=-\frac{s}{\omega_3}L_\phi\longrightarrow0.$$ Every full cut has its three-dimensional area element multiplied by $e^{3s\phi}$; the cut class itself is unchanged. Taking infima yields <a id="n4:eq:strictification-area"></a>$$\label{n4:eq:strictification-area}
 A_*(g)\le A_*(g_s)\le e^{3s\|\phi\|_\infty}A_*(g).$$ The infimum is finite, since a distant coordinate sphere is admissible. Its convergence as $s\downarrow0$ follows without an attained minimizer. Together these estimates prove every asserted output at this fixed rest datum. If it is $(g_R,K_R)$, every constant above may depend on $R$; strictification is removed with $R$ fixed. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-64"></a>
#### Applying the prepared theorem and returning to the original end

The proper radial comparison protects the original enclosing area during rest-end replacement. Strictification then changes the cut infimum by a factor tending to one at each fixed replacement radius. We apply the prepared inequality after both constructions, remove strictification at that fixed radius, and finally send the replacement radius to infinity.

<a id="stmt-n4-end-transfer"></a>
<div id="n4:end:transfer" class="proposition">

**Proposition 57** (Transfer from prepared data). *Theorem <a href="#thm:numerical:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:numerical:prepared">8</a>, applied in dimension four, implies Theorem <a href="#n4:thm:weak" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:thm:weak">49</a>.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n4-end-transfer"><summary>Proof of stmt-n4-end-transfer</summary>

<a id="n4:end:one-sided-area"></a>
*Proof.* First let the original exterior have one end and $E>|P|$. Set $m=(E^2-|P|^2)^{1/2}>0$. Proposition <a href="#n4:prop:rest-end" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:prop:rest-end">55</a> gives data $(g_R,K_R)$ with zero momentum and energy $m_R\to m$. Its full-cut comparison is $$\label{n4:end:one-sided-area}
 A_*(g_R)\ge(1+\epsilon_R)^{-3/2}A_*(g),
 \qquad \epsilon_R\longrightarrow0.$$ Fix one sufficiently large replacement radius $R$. For any fixed $0<\delta_1<1$, Lemma <a href="#n4:lem:strictification" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:lem:strictification">56</a> makes $(g_{R,s},K_{R,s})$ a prepared exterior for all sufficiently small $s>0$. Indeed it is the same smooth connected orientable one-ended exterior, complete with its compact boundary included and with compact complement of its coordinate end. It has finite ADM energy and a compactly supported tensor, so its ADM momentum is zero. On the end, $g_{R,s}-\delta=O_d(r^{-2})$ for every fixed derivative order $d$, its scalar curvature is $O(r^{-4-\delta_1})$, and its constraint densities are integrable. The boundary is strictly future trapped, and the global margin is $$\mu_{R,s}-|J_{R,s}|_{g_{R,s}}
 \ge c_{R,s}\rho^{-4-\delta_1},\qquad c_{R,s}>0,$$ where $\rho$ is a positive smooth extension of the rest-end radius. These are the geometric and decay conditions of Definition <a href="#def:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:prepared">6</a>, with $n=4$ and $\beta=\delta_1$.

The area condition follows along the same comparisons. In one end, Definition <a href="#n4:def:cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:def:cuts">48</a> is exactly the prepared full-cut class: the outer domain is connected and closed, its interior lies in the open exterior, and its entire compact intrinsic boundary is counted, including every component and all coincidence with the original boundary. Lemma <a href="#n4:lem:cut-reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:lem:cut-reduction">50</a> gives $A_*(g)>0$; Equation <a href="#n4:end:one-sided-area" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:end:one-sided-area">[n4:end:one-sided-area]</a> and strictification give $A_*(g_{R,s})\ge A_*(g_R)>0$. The constraint and ADM normalizations also agree: $2\mu=R+(\operatorname{tr}K)^2-|K|^2$, $J=\operatorname{div}(K-(\operatorname{tr}K)g)$, and the energy and momentum factors are $1/(6\omega_3)$ and $1/(3\omega_3)$. No rescaling is made.

Theorem <a href="#thm:numerical:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:numerical:prepared">8</a> therefore yields, at every such fixed pair $(R,s)$, <a id="n4:end:fixed-prepared-inequality"></a>$$\label{n4:end:fixed-prepared-inequality}
 E_{R,s}\ge\frac12
       \left(\frac{A_*(g_{R,s})}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}.$$ This is the completed numerical theorem: its elliptic exhaustion and its limits $N\to\infty$ and $\epsilon\downarrow0$ have already been taken for the fixed prepared datum. None of those estimates is required to be uniform in $R$ or $s$.

<a id="n4:end:timelike-conclusion"></a>
Now let $s\downarrow0$ with $R$ fixed. Strictification gives both $E_{R,s}\to m_R$ and $A_*(g_{R,s})\to A_*(g_R)$, so $$m_R\ge\frac12
       \left(\frac{A_*(g_R)}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}
 \ge\frac12(1+\epsilon_R)^{-1}
       \left(\frac{A_*(g)}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}.$$ Only at this point let $R\to\infty$. The result is $$\label{n4:end:timelike-conclusion}
 \sqrt{E^2-|P|^2}\ge\frac12
       \left(\frac{A_*(g)}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}
       \qquad (E>|P|).$$ Full convergence of $A_*(g_R)$ has not been used or asserted.

It remains to remove the timelike assumption. If instead $E\le|P|$, take any sequence $a_j>0$ tending to zero and set $$\lambda_j=\frac{|P|+a_j-E}{2}>0.$$ Lemma <a href="#n4:end:positive-shell" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:end:positive-shell">52</a> gives, separately for each $j$, data of energy $|P|+a_j$, momentum $P$, and enclosing infimum at least $A_*(g)$. Their charges are future timelike, so <a href="#n4:end:timelike-conclusion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:end:timelike-conclusion">[n4:end:timelike-conclusion]</a> gives $$\sqrt{(|P|+a_j)^2-|P|^2}
 \ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_*(g)}{\omega_3}\right)^{2/3}>0.$$ The right side is fixed and positive by Lemma <a href="#n4:lem:cut-reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:lem:cut-reduction">50</a>, while the left side tends to zero. This contradiction includes zero, negative, and null energy cases. No preparation geometry is passed to a limit as the boost degenerates: the timelike numerical result was applied afresh to each shell datum. Thus $E>|P|$ and <a href="#n4:end:timelike-conclusion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:end:timelike-conclusion">[n4:end:timelike-conclusion]</a> hold for every one-ended original datum in the theorem.

Finally let the original manifold have finitely many ends and fix one end $e$. Truncate every other end at a sufficiently large sphere as in Lemma <a href="#n4:lem:cut-reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:lem:cut-reduction">50</a>. The retained manifold is a complete connected one-ended exterior. Its added boundary components are strictly future trapped, its selected-end charges are still $(E_e,P_e)$, and its full-cut infimum is at least $A_e(S)$. Applying the one-ended result gives $$E_e\ge\sqrt{|P_e|^2+
              \frac14\left(\frac{A_e(S)}{\omega_3}\right)^{4/3}}.$$ Positivity of $A_e(S)$ was proved before any truncation. This gives both the asserted inequality and strict future timelikeness at $e$. ◻

</details>

The one-ended cases of Theorems <a href="#thm:weak3" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:weak3">45</a> and <a href="#n4:thm:weak" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:thm:weak">49</a> together prove Theorem <a href="#thm:low" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:low">5</a>.

<a id="pm-h-65"></a>
#### The general maximal DEC energy inequality

The maximal special case requires no assumption that a momentum limit exists. The following end calculation supplies that limit from the decay and integrability already imposed on the data.

<a id="stmt-n4-lem-momentum-exists"></a>
<div id="n4:lem:momentum-exists" class="lemma">

**Lemma 58** (Existence of the momentum flux). *On a smooth four-dimensional asymptotically flat end, suppose $g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q})$ and $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$ for some $q>1$. If $|J|_g$ is integrable, where $J_i=\nabla^j(K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij})$, then each ADM momentum limit in <a href="#n4:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:intro:momentum">[n4:intro:momentum]</a> exists and is finite.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n4-lem-momentum-exists"><summary>Proof of stmt-n4-lem-momentum-exists</summary>

<a id="n4:end:momentum-integrability"></a>
*Proof.* In the given coordinates set $$\pi^g_{ij}=K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g_{ij},\qquad
 \pi^\delta_{ij}=K_{ij}-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\delta K)\delta_{ij}.$$ The differentiated decay assumptions give $$\label{n4:end:momentum-integrability}
 \pi^g-\pi^\delta=O_1(r^{-1-2q}),\qquad
 \partial_j\pi^\delta_{ij}-J_i=O(r^{-2-2q}).$$ To verify the second bound, expand the covariant divergence as $$J_i=g^{jk}\bigl(\partial_k\pi^g_{ij}
       -\Gamma^a_{ki}\pi^g_{aj}-\Gamma^a_{kj}\pi^g_{ia}\bigr).$$ Replacing $g^{jk}$ by $\delta^{jk}$ costs $O(r^{-q})O(r^{-2-q})$; replacing $\pi^g$ by $\pi^\delta$ costs the derivative of the first bound in <a href="#n4:end:momentum-integrability" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:end:momentum-integrability">[n4:end:momentum-integrability]</a>. Each connection term has size $O(r^{-1-q})O(r^{-1-q})$. These are exactly the asserted errors.

Their Euclidean radial volume bound is $Cr^{1-2q}$, integrable because $q>1$. The asymptotic metric and Euclidean volume and covector norms are uniformly comparable, so $\partial_j\pi^\delta_{ij}\in L^1$. The Euclidean divergence theorem between two large spheres makes the flux $\int_{S_R}\pi^\delta_{ij}n_\delta^j\,\,\mathrm dA_\delta$ a Cauchy function of $R$, with finite limit. By the first bound in <a href="#n4:end:momentum-integrability" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:end:momentum-integrability">[n4:end:momentum-integrability]</a>, its difference from the flux of $\pi^g$ is $O(R^{2-2q})\to0$. This is the tensor appearing in <a href="#n4:intro:momentum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:intro:momentum">[n4:intro:momentum]</a>, which proves the lemma. ◻

</details>

<a id="stmt-n4-ass-energy"></a>
<div id="n4:ass:energy" class="corollary">

**Corollary 59** (Maximal DEC energy inequality). *<span id="n4:cor:maximal-dec" label="n4:cor:maximal-dec"></span>Let $(X^4,g_X,K_X)$ be smooth and connected, with $X$ orientable, $g_X$ complete as a metric space with its nonempty compact smooth boundary $S_X$ included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat and diffeomorphic to the complement of a closed ball in $\mathbb R^4$. Let $K_X$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor. Suppose $$\begin{gathered}
 \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{g_X}K_X=0,\qquad
 \mu_X=\tfrac12(R_{g_X}-|K_X|_{g_X}^2)
       \ge|\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_{g_X}K_X|_{g_X},\\
 \mu_X,|\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_{g_X}K_X|_{g_X}\in L^1(X,\,\mathrm dV_{g_X}).
\end{gathered}$$ Assume for some $q>1$ that $$g_X-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K_X=O_1(r^{-1-q}),$$ and that the ADM energy $E_X$ in <a href="#n4:intro:energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="n4:intro:energy">[n4:intro:energy]</a> is finite. On every component of $S_X$, require $H+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{S_X}K_X\le0$ with the normal into $X$. For the one-ended enclosing-cut infimum of Definition <a href="#n4:def:cuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:def:cuts">48</a>, denoted here by $a_{g_X}(S_X)$, one has $$E_X\ge\frac12\left(\frac{a_{g_X}(S_X)}{2\pi^2}\right)^{2/3}.$$ The boundary may have any topology and finitely many components. No symmetry, vacuum, spin, outermostness, outer area-minimization or momentum-flux assumption is imposed.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-n4-ass-energy"><summary>Proof of stmt-n4-ass-energy</summary>

*Proof.* Maximality identifies the momentum density with $J_X=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_{g_X}K_X$. Lemma <a href="#n4:lem:momentum-exists" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:lem:momentum-exists">58</a> supplies the finite ADM momentum. All hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#n4:thm:weak" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:thm:weak">49</a> therefore hold for this one-ended exterior. Its invariant-mass inequality in particular gives the displayed energy bound. The proof of Theorem <a href="#n4:thm:weak" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="n4:thm:weak">49</a> uses Theorem <a href="#thm:numerical:prepared" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:numerical:prepared">8</a>, independently of this corollary. This numerical consequence retains its broad maximal-DEC scope; the separate direct maximal-vacuum construction has its own hypotheses. ◻

</details>

    {
      "caption": "The two densities at a hypothetical contact point $p ∈ supp |D1_{FN}| ∩ ∂O_{N}$, with $z ∈ C_{N}^{h}$ chosen so that $d_{g}(z,p) = s = s_{N}$. The circles depict background metric balls schematically; no regularity of the obstacle or of the contact is assumed. Their overlap provides the first density. Minimality provides the second. Relative isoperimetry then forces perimeter inside the large constant conformal plateau, contradicting the competitor bound.",
      "figure_id": "fig:height:two-densities",
      "pdf_page": 61,
      "source_evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "fig:height:two-densities",
          "exact_quote": "The two densities at a hypothetical contact point\n$p\\in\\supp|D\\mathbf1_{F_N}|\\cap\\partial O_N$, with $z\\in C_N^h$ chosen so that $d_g(z,p)=s=s_N$.\nThe circles depict background metric balls schematically; no regularity\nof the obstacle or of",
          "source_object": "fig:0001"
        }
      ],
      "source_kind": "tikz_pgf",
      "tikz_pgf_source": "\\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.92,>=Stealth,\n  every node/.style={font=\\small}]\n  \\fill[blue!9] (0,0) circle[radius=1.65];\n  \\draw[blue!55!black,thick] (0,0) circle[radius=1.65];\n  \\draw[orange!65!black,thick,dashed] (1.65,0) circle[radius=1.65];\n  \\fill[blue!40] (0.825,0) circle[radius=0.4125];\n  \\draw[blue!60!black] (0.825,0) circle[radius=0.4125];\n  \\draw[black!65] (0,0)--(1.65,0);\n  \\node[font=\\scriptsize,fill=blue!9,inner sep=1pt] at (0.50,0.78) {$d_g(z,p)=s$};\n  \\fill (0,0) circle[radius=0.035] node[below left] {$z$};\n  \\fill (0.825,0) circle[radius=0.035];\n  \\fill (1.65,0) circle[radius=0.045] node[below right] {$p$};\n  \\node[blue!55!black,align=center] at (-0.55,1.90)\n    {$B_s^g(z)\\subset O_N$};\n  \\node[orange!65!black] at (2.27,1.90) {$B_s^g(p)$};\n  \\draw[->,blue!60!black] (0.78,-1.78)--(0.825,-0.46);\n  \\node[align=center,anchor=north] at (0.78,-1.90)\n    {a ball of radius $s/4$\\\\inside both balls};\n  \\node[align=left,anchor=west] at (4.0,0.4)\n    {Obstacle inclusion gives\\\\\n     $\\Vol_g(F_N\\cap B_s^g(p))\\ge c s^n$.\\\\[7pt]\n     Filling-ball comparison gives\\\\\n     $\\Vol_g(F_N^c\\cap B_s^g(p))\\ge e^{-P_N}s^n$.};\n\\end{tikzpicture}",
      "witness_description": "A schematic geometric diagram showing two overlapping circles: on the left, a solid circle centered at point $z$ labeled $B_s^g(z) \\subset O_N$; on the right, a dashed circle centered at point $p$ labeled $B_s^g(p)$. A line segment connects $z$ and $p$ labeled $d_g(z, p) = s$. Within the intersection of the two circles is a shaded circular region with an arrow indicating \"a ball of radius $s/4$ inside both balls\". To the right of the circles are two formula blocks: \"Obstacle inclusion gives $\\mathrm{Vol}_g(F_N \\cap B_s^g(p)) \\ge c s^n$.\" and \"Filling-ball comparison gives $\\mathrm{Vol}_g(F_N^c \\cap B_s^g(p)) \\ge e^{-P_N} s^n$.\""
    }
